A_Distribution: Currently only found in Sichuan, Gansu and Xiaxi, China.
A_Habitat: The Giant Panda is found on mountains between the elevations of 2,600 to 3,000 with the actual elevation changing depending on the season. Areas with clean, running water and well-developed bamboo groves are favored.
A_Feature:
1. Adults measure between 120 to 180 cm in height, and 80 to 120 kg in weight. Cubs measure around 10 cm in length and weigh just 150 to 200 grams at birth.
2. Powerful limbs: The hindlegs are turned inwards for pulling bamboo out of the way when moving through dense forests.
3. The wrist bone has evolved into a pseudo-thumb (with no joints) for grasping and eating bamboo.
4. The paws are covered with fur for walking over cold snow.
4. The Giant Panda is black and white in color. The ears, eye patch, nose, shoulders and limbs are black while the rest of the body is white. The small, black ears reduce heat loss.
A_Behavior:
1. Giant Pandas are solitary animals except for mating or a mother with her cub.
2. Bamboo contains very little calories so giant pandas spend around 10 hours a day asleep to conserve energy. They generally forage around dawn and dusk.
A_Diet: Bamboo makes up more than 99% of the giant panda's diet.
A_Crisis: The variety of bamboo species in the Giant Panda habitat was once relatively limited. The cyclical flowering and mass die-off of arrow bamboo in 1983 for example led to pandas in the region starving to death. Bamboo forests also take many years to recover after floowering. Habitat fragmention prevents pandas from migrating to new sources of bamboo and increases the risk of inbreeding as well.

A_Distribution: Sub-antarctic region. Found in South America at the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the Sandwich Islands, as well as the waters south of South Africa and New Zealand.
A_Feature: The King Penguin is one of the largest species of penguins second only to the Emperor Penguin in size. They have a long beak and an orange-colored ear patch. The ear patch has a black border and is shaped like a water drop. The area between the throat and chest is a beautiful golden yellow color. Body measures approximately 95cm in length (penguins’ body length is measured from the beak to the extended tail). Body weight is around 12 to 15 kg. It can live between 15 to 20 years on average in captivity.
A_Behavior:
1. King penguins live on average between 15 to 20 years in captivity.
2. King penguins form breeding colonies during which each pair claim a territory of one square meter for their own. No nest is built and only one egg is laid by each pair. The male and female take turns incubating the egg and this takes about 56 days. Chicks are almost nude but covered only by some short down. The down starts out as light gray or brown then gradually turns dark brown. At around 40 days the chicks join a cr?che with other chicks. They becomes fully fledged between 10 to 13 months, and reach sexual maturity between 5 to 7 years.
3. The population of King Penguin is around 2 million in the wild and is still increasing (based on 2008 assessment conducted by International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)).
A_Diet: Diet consists mainly of fish. In the wild, King Penguin are fond of small lantern fishes (Myctophidae) but will also eat squids (Moroteuthis) and other cephalopods.

A_Distribution: South Africa and Namibia.
A_Habitat: Jackass Penguins live on land in the sea. They generally nest on islands near the shore but will occassionally nest on continental coasts. Foraging takes place on the open sea.
A_Feature: Jackass Penguins have a black cheek and a broad white stripe that runs from the brow to the head. There is a reddish area in front of the eyes. Some birds have a second black stripe on their upper chest. The heads of juveniles are gray in color and the chest stripe is indistinct. Body measures between 68 to 70 cm in length. Body weight is around 2 to 3 kg.
A_Behavior:
1. Gregarious. They are curious, timid but cautious.
2. Large growling sounds are usually made during arguments or courtship.
3. As temperate zone penguins they have several tricks for keeping cool: The feathers are thin and fluffy, and there is only a thin layer of subcutaneous fat. On land, they look for sheltered locations. They also gasp through their mouths for heat dissipation.
4. Jackass Penguins breed all year round. They usually nest under rocks, inside bushes, or in holes. The nest is usually lined in some way. There are 2 eggs per clutch. A second clutch has also been recorded. Incubation period is around 38 days.
A_Diet: In the wild, Jackass Penguins catch and eat fishes between 0.5 ~ 1.2cm in length in the open sea. The main prey species are anchovies and herrings. They dive up to 130m in pursuit of prey, with gathering in the open sea to catch fish cooperatively.
A_Crisis: At the beginning of the 20th century, there were estimated to be 500,000 to 1,000,000 pairs of Jackass Penguins in existence. Current population is estimated to be 50,000 (based on 2018 assessment conducted by International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)). The main reason for their population decline is the industrialized harvesting of the fish they eat and it is impossible to estimate how many are caught up in fishing nets.

A_Distribution: Tropical rainforests of Borneo.
A_Habitat: Tropical rainforests and secondary forests at low elevations.
A_Feature:
1. Its entire body is covered with reddish-brown hair. The color of the coarse, sparse strands of hair change with age as well. Juveniles have bright orange fur, while adults have reddish-brown fur. Some individuals can even have dark chocolate-brown fur.
2. The hair on the top of a young ape's head is erect and becomes flattened upon maturity. Areas around the nose, mouth and eyes of a young ape are pink, but become black or light brown when it becomes an adult.
2. Adult males are about double the size of females. Males have long, reddish-brown hair, bulging cheek flaps, and a hanging throat sack. The orangutan's forelimbs are longer than its rear limbs. Its fingers and toes are long and curved. 
3. Adult females have a high forehead, protruding nose and mouth, and a smaller throat sac. The hair on the side of a female's face and on top of its head is shorter.
A_Behavior:
1. It is diurnal but most active in the morning and around dusk.
2. Its fingers and toes are quite strong and are used for picking fruit and hanging onto branches. It can swing from branch to branch using its arms as well.
3. It rarely comes down to the ground. The young learn the techniques of swinging through the trees from their mother. On the ground, it walks with all fours slowly and cautiously, with its knuckles touching the ground.
4. Every night, it will build a nest out of leaves and branches in a tree for sleeping. Old nests are used during the day for naps. When it rains or when the sun is too strong, it will use a leafy branch for shade or hang large leaves around its neck. It knows how to use branches for digging, fighting, scratching and eating.
5. Orangutans are relatively quiet compared to other primates. Adult males are usually solitary and use their throat sac as a resonator to make calls through the jungle. These calls are used to assert their territory and for courtship.
6. Females have a strong maternal instinct and will care for a young until it achieves full independence before mating and giving birth again. Young orangutans rely almost entirely on their mother for breastfeeding and for feeding before the age of 2 or 3. From the age of 4, a young orangutan learns how to live in the rainforest from its mother. When females reach maturity they tend to stay close to their mother.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, mainly diet on leaves, bark, and fruit such as figs, rambutan, etc. They may also eat insects, small invertebrates, bird eggs, and soil rich in minerals.
A_Crisis: Loss of habitat, poaching, forest fire, habitat fragmentation

A_Distribution: Rainforests and dense forests in Malaysia (Malay Peninsula), Indonesia (Sumatra), and southern Thailand.
A_Habitat: Tropical deciduous and evergreen rainforests between 600 to 2,000 m above sea level.
A_Feature:
1. The siamang is the largest of the lesser apes. Thick, black fur covers its body. Males have fur that's about 15 cm long around their scrotum. One weighs between 10 to 12 kg and measures between 71 to 90 cm from head to rump. Its fully extended arms are about 2.3 to 2.6 times the length of its body.
2. Their 2nd and 3rd toes fused by a thin webbing of skin.
3. Both the male and the female have gray or pink throat sacs. The throat sacs balloon when they are vocalizing.
A_Behavior:
1. It is diurnal, but is more active in the morning than afternoon. It returns at dusk every day to a specific tree to sleep.
2. It is arboreal and spends most of its time in the trees, 25 to 30 m above ground. It climbs with its forelimbs with great agility, and rarely leaves the trees.
3. It is monogamous. Each family has a territory that they assert through their calls. They spend about 30% of each day calling loudly, with the male making shrieks and the females making a series of howls as long as 18 s. Bonds are strong between family members, and they gather on the same tree or group of trees to forage and groom each other.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, mainly diet on leaves , fruits and flowers, shoots, insects.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, poaching, forest fire, and habitat fragmentation.

A_Distribution: India, the Indochina Peninsula, the Malay Peninsula, and Sumatra.
A_Habitat: Tropical evergreen and deciduous forests.
A_Feature:
Hornbill beaks have a distinct feature called a casque on top of its massive bill, casque is covered with keratin and usually hollow, reinforced by bony honeycomb-like struts which keeps the bird light for flight. Its head looks as if it's wearing a helmet. 
2. Its feathers are mostly black, and its tail is long and wide with a black band. 
3. Males and females can be distinguished by the color of their irises. Females have white irises, while that of the males are red.
A_Behavior:
1. It is a tree-dwelling bird that lives in pairs or as a family group in the rainforest. It builds its nests in tree holes.

2. During the breeding season, the female stays with her hatchlings inside their tree-hole nest. The entrance is sealed with mud, leaving only a small hole through which the male delivers food for the entire family. The hole is used by the female and the hatchlings for defecation as well.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, mostly diet on fruits, small animals such as frogs, lizards, bird hatchlings, snails, and insects.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, poaching, forest fire, and habitat fragmentation.

A_Distribution: India and parts of Southeast Asia including Sumatra and Borneo.
A_Habitat: Grasslands, tropical evergreen forests, and bushlands.
A_Feature:
1. Its massive body is dark-grey, and it has a large head and thick, strong limbs.
2. Compared to the African elephant, the Asiatic elephant has smaller ears, a rounded back, and a finger-like protrusion on the tip of its nose. The protrusion contains a large number of nerve cells, giving the trunk a dexterity similar to that of a human finger.
3. The outward apperence of front legs have five toe nails each, and the rear legs have four each. There are two semicircular protrusions on the front edge of the skull.
4. Females may not have tusks, and even if they do, their tusks would not be pronounced. Male elephants are larger than females.
A_Behavior:
1. It is mainly active at dawn, dusk, and at night. It generally stays in the forest and cool, shady areas during the daytime. The Asian elephant is not as resistant to heat as the African elephant.
2. It loves mud and dirt baths as mud protects from the sun and parasites. Asian elephants usually live in regions with a plentiful supply of water, and where the grass that makes up the bulk of their diet grows in abundance. An elephant spends more than two-thirds of its day foraging. 
3. The temporal gland between the eyes and the ears of a male elephant produces oily secretions when it is in estrus. Males become very restless during this time.
3. Asian elephants live in matriarchal herds. Each herd may contain anywhere from several to dozens of members led by the eldest female. They do not stay in a fixed area and therefore have a widespread distribution.
4. Ivory refers to the incisors on the elephant's upper jaw and is one of the key features of a male elephant. Ivory is used for stripping tree bark and digging up roots. It is also a symbol of social status and a weapon with which to attack the enemy.
5. Elephant molars wear away quite quickly as they are used for chewing hard foods such as tree bark. New molars grow and replace old molars. An elephant may have six sets of molars during its lifetime.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, including grass, leaves, bark, shrub, such as banana trees, sugar cane, and fruit.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, and habitat fragmentation.

A_Distribution: India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, and China.
A_Habitat: Rainforests, forests, mangroves, swamps, grasslands, and rocky regions.
A_Feature: 1. Its body is yellow or yellow-brown and is covered in narrow black stripes, which are denser around the head. The abdomen is white. The back of the ears is black with white spots. The tail is  with several black rings.
A_Behavior:
1. It is active at dusk and at night, though occasionally during the daytime as well.
2. Tigers are solitary unless it is a mother and her young. Solitary tigers, however, still maintain contact with their neighbors. Tigers communicate through sound and scent. Its anal glands secrete a substance with intense scent, which it uses for marking its territory and presence.
3. Females in estrus cycle will become very active and vocal to attract a male.
4. Tigers are excellent swimmers. They will jump into the water to stay cool on a hot day.
5. Tigers have a superb hearing, sharp fangs, and retractable claws. The stripes on their body provide camouflage. These adaptations make them the apex predator of the forest.
A_Diet: Carnivorous, the majority of the tiger diet consists of various large ungulate species such as  deers, water buffalo, boars, bears,  or  smaller mammals such as muntjac and birds.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, poaching, forest fire, and habitat fragmentation.

A_Distribution: Widely distributed in the forests, grasslands, and bushlands of Africa, the Middle East, as well as the eastern, southwestern and southern parts of Asia.
A_Habitat: Variety habitats, including lowland forests, mountain ridges, grasslands, bushlands, and deserts.
A_Feature:
1. Its yellowish-brown body is covered with hollow black markings. Its belly is white with black spots. All leopards have spots on their face. The spotted pattern is unique for each leopard.
2. Some leopards are entirely black, a black  panther . It's not a separate species. It is black only because its genes for fur color happen to be recessive. If you examine a black  panther closely under good lighting, you'll see that they have spotted fur.
A_Behavior:
1. It is nocturnal and solitary unless it's a mother and her cubs.
2. Leopards can adapt to different environments, as long as there are enough prey and cover, but they prefer forested areas. They are very agile and are adept climbers. They can swim but will generally stay away from water. Unlike tigers, leopards do not like to get wet and tend to lead a more arboreal existence.
3. The leopard has excellent eyes and ears. They will pounce on their prey from a tree and will sometimes drag their prey back into the tree to eat. They usually feed on the abdomen of the prey first. When the leopard finishes eating the organs and limbs, the leopard will store the leftovers on the fork of a tree with dense covering.
A_Diet: Carnivorous and preys on small mammals.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, decrease in prey numbers, habitat fragmentation, and poaching.

A_Distribution: Myanmar, the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo.
A_Habitat: Dense forests in the tropical and subtropical regions.
A_Feature:
1. It is the smallest member of the bear family (Ursidae).
2. It has a short and broad head with round and small ears. Its body is covered in black, glossy fur. There is a white or pale yellow U-shaped patch on its chest.
3. Its four claws are curved inwards like sickles. The soles are furless, which helps it climb trees.
4. Its tongue is between 20 to 25 cm in length. The long tongue helps the sun bear feed on honey and termites with ease.
A_Behavior:
1. It is nocturnal, does not hibernate, and is a superb tree climber. It usually spends its daytime in a tree nest sun-basking or sleeping. It is most active between 2 to 7 m above the forest floor.
2. It has an excellent sense of smell. In the wild, the sun bear consumes a variety of fruits, including wild durian, rambutan, and figs. It will swallow seeds as well, and the seeds will leave the bear's digestive tract  with its feces far away from the parent plant. This greatly increases the survival rate of the seeds, as it does not need to compete with its parent plant.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, diet on fruits, small mammals, birds, and invertebrates such as millipedes, worms, beetle larvae, and termites.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, habitat fragmentation, poaching

A_Distribution: Throughout Southeast Asia, from southern Myanmar to Thailand, the Malay Peninsula, and Sumatra.
A_Habitat: Primary forests, secondary forests, the forest edge, and swamps.
A_Feature:
1. The fur on its trunk and rump are white while the rest is black. Its ears are erect with white tips.
2. Newborn Malayan tapirs are dark brown white stripes and spots. This natural camouflage helps them blend in with the scattered sunlight and shade on the rainforest floor. The brown fur and patterning on young tapirs gradually fade away after three months, and they become black and white like the adults.
A_Behavior:
1. It is a solitary species. Its stubby tail is held erect when urinating. The urine is sprayed in a cone pattern and is a territorial marking behavior.
2. When threatened, it dashes out of the jungle and dives into water where it uses its nose as a snorkel or stays fully submerged for over half a minute until the enemy leaves. If there is no water nearby, then it will sit down and pretend to be a rock to avoid attention.
A_Diet: Omnivorous and eats buds, leaves, fruits, grass and aquatic plants.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, habitat fragmentation, and poaching.

A_Distribution: Least Concern (LC)
A_Habitat: Southeast and southwest Australia.
A_Feature: Large lakes and shallow lagoons.
A_Behavior:
1. It is the only swan with black feathers. However, when it extends its wings, its primary and secondary feathers are all white. Its beak is bright red while its feet are grayish-black.
2. Males are slightly larger than females. A female's pupils and beak are also slightly less vivid - either pink or light pink. Young swans' pupils are grayish-brown in color and their beaks are of a paler shade.
A_Diet:
1. Black swans favor large lakes or shallow lagoons. They are very gregarious and have no fixed territory. They form large breeding flocks and live in groups as well outside the breeding season.
2. They are seasonal breeders. During breeding season, the male and female build a nest together using twigs and leaves on floating plants or the water's edge. Once the eggs are laid, the female incubates them while the male stands guard, or they take shifts.
A_Crisis: Entirely herbivorous, mainly on aquatic plants, algae and grass. Most of its food is found in the water, but it will also forage on pastures or water-logged fields.

A_Distribution: Bolivia, Peru, and parts of Brazil in South America.
A_Habitat: Lives in tropical rainforests, grasslands, farmland, wetlands, and river regions.
A_Feature:
1. Its fur is short, dense, and very soft. Its mouth and nose are black and hairless. The area around the eyes, ears, throat, and side of the neck are white. Its head is a deep, grayish-black that is darker than that of the squirrel monkey. Its back is brown, limbs are reddish-brown or yellow, flanks are grayish-white, and its tail tip is black.
2. Its large eyes are placed close together. It has large ears, relatively short thumbs, long tails, and the tail tip is slightly fluffy.
3. Its body measures about 30cm in the length, and weighs around 1,000g. Its tail is about 40cm long.
A_Behavior:
1. They are diurnal animals that are most active in the trees, but will occasionally come down to the ground.
2. They are social animals. Adult males will fight to establish their social hierarchy during the mating season.
3. They have a variety of calls. Different calls are used for greetings, alerts, mating, attacks, or when in pain.
A_Diet: It is omnivorous and feeds on fruits, strawberries, nuts, flowers, flower buds, seeds, insects, and small vertebrates. It will also drink nectar if other food is unavailable.

A_Distribution: Southern Panama, northern Ecuador, and Colombia.
A_Habitat: Lives in rainforests or mountain forests.
A_Feature:
1. It has coarse, dark, black fur and a small, whiskered head. The skin on its face is black. Its thumbs are not dexterous enough for gripping objects because they have degenerated. It has slender limbs that make it well-suited for hanging from trees.
2. The underside of its tip tail has no fur growing. The tail is prehensile with an excellent sense of touch. The monkey can often be seen hanging from branches by one leg and the tail as if it has a fifth hand.
A_Behavior:
1. Spider monkeys are diurnal, social animals that live in rainforests or mountain forests. They usually move between trees in the forest canopy with great agility.
2. Its mating season is not definite, and females give birth once every two to four years.
A_Diet: It feeds mainly on fruits but will also eat nuts, seeds, flowers and flower buds, leaves, insects, spiders, and bird eggs.

A_Distribution: Mainly in the eastern and southwestern parts of Australia.
A_Habitat: Cold, wet forests with dense or medium foliage.
A_Feature:
1. It is the largest member of the kingfisher family (Alcedinidae). The feathers on its head and chest are beige or white, while its wings are brownish-black. A pale blue stripe runs along the outer margin of its wings, and a brown stripe extends from its beak up to the top of its head, or over its eyes to its cheeks. Its beak is boat-shaped. The root of the tail on males is usually blue, though both males and females have red and black stripes on their tails. The tail tip is white.
2. Females are slightly larger than males.
A_Behavior:
1. It is very territorial and will call at dawn or dusk to assert territory. It may also call to express anxiety or excitement. Its call sounds like a boisterous human laughing.
2. It is a social animal. A group may consist of one to five families. Young birds will stay with their group and help care for their newborn siblings when they grow up.
3. Kookaburras hunt by perching on a high spot and staying motionless. A kookaburra will dive down and snatch its prey with its beak before flying back up to their perch, and banging its prey against a tree trunk to kill it and to soften it. The prey is then swallowed whole, headfirst.
A_Diet: Mainly diet on rodents, lizards, snakes, large insects, and fish.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, and habitat fragmentation.

A_Distribution: Central America south of Mexico.
A_Habitat: Mainly lives in the canopy of tropical rainforests in South America.
A_Feature:
1. Its arms are slightly longer and stronger than its legs. Its tail can wrap dexterously around tree branches like a fifth hand.
2. Females are often mistaken for males due to their large engorged clitoris.
A_Behavior:
1. It mainly lives in the forest canopy and generally feeds at dawn.
2. It has a prehensile tail. Its thumb has undergone devolution, but the other fingers are slender and strong. These adaptations allow the animal to swing between branches in the rainforest.
A_Diet: Its diet consists mainly of fruits and nuts. It will also eat leaves, small insects, bird eggs, and honey.

A_Distribution: Brazil and its neighboring countries in South America.
A_Habitat: Mainly found in the rivers, ponds, and marshes of South America.
A_Feature:
1. The capybara is the largest rodent in the world and can weigh up to 70kg.
2. Its front legs are slightly shorter than its rear legs, and its feet are partially webbed.
A_Behavior:
1. They may look bulky but are actually agile. They can run very fast on land and are quite agile in the water as well.
2. A clan is usually made of 10 to 20 members, led by an alpha male.
A_Diet: It lives mainly on aquatic plants, bark, grass, and fruits.
A_Crisis: Although the capybara is frequently hunted for its meat and fur, fortunately, they are fast-breeders and live mostly in protected regions, so the species is currently not threatened.

A_Distribution: From Honduras in Central America to northern Argentina in South America.
A_Habitat: Lives mainly in grasslands or forests.
A_Feature:
1. Its body length measures between 180 to 200 cm and weigh between 30 to 60 kg.
2. It has a slender head with very small eyes and ears. Its snout is shaped like a tube.
3. Its magnificent tail is long and fanned like a broom, with long, stiff hairs that aid help it balance.
A_Behavior:
1. Though toothless, it has a tongue of more than 60cm long for eating ants and small invertebrates.
2. It uses its tail as a blanket to cover its body when it is sleeping.
A_Diet: It feeds mainly on ants, terminates, and small invertebrates.

A_Distribution: Brazil and its neighboring countries in South America.
A_Habitat: Lives on the forest floor and understory near rivers.
A_Feature:
1. Coloration varies depending on geographical region and includes pale yellow, brown, or grayish-white. 
2. It has small eyes, large ears, and a very long, probing nose. The tip of the nose has a small opening as wide as a pencil, from which a long tongue emerges to lick up ants.
3. Its prehensile tail acts as a strong fifth hand for climbing.
4. Its body length measures between 30 to 80cm, and the tail is 40 to 70cm long.
A_Behavior:
1. It prefers to be active at dusk and is an excellent tree-climber.
2. Its thick, strong forelimbs and claws are used to tear open anthills.
3. Its eyesight is weak, so it uses hearing and smell to locate termites, ants, bees, and honey to feed on.
4. It likes to sleep during the day.
A_Diet: It feeds mainly on ants and termites.

A_Distribution: Panama in Central America, as well as coastal regions of Colombia and Ecuador in South America.
A_Habitat: Lives in forest canopy.
A_Feature:
1. Its face, throat, and chest are white and rest of the body being black. Its body and tail are extra furry.
2. The semi-prehensile tail is usually curled up. (It is semi-prehensile because it can be used for support but not for holding objects)
A_Behavior: The white-faced Capuchin is a diurnal tree-dweller. It can adapt to different-type forests, including secondary forests and seaside mangroves.
A_Diet: It is omnivorous and feeds on fruits, berries, nuts, seeds, flowers, flower buds, leaves, bark, insects, spiders, small vertebrates, and bird eggs. Individuals living by the seaside will also eat crabs and shells.

A_Distribution: Colombia and parts of Venezuela in South America.
A_Habitat: Lives in rainforest canopy.
A_Feature:
1. Its body color ranges from pale to dark brown. Most individuals have a white triangle on their foreheads.
2. It has slender limbs and a powerful tail that allow them to move easily through the forest.
3. The thumbs on the forelimbs have degenerated into a bony nub, leaving only four fingers.
A_Behavior: Brown spider monkeys are highly social animals. During the day, large clans split into several small groups to search for food.
A_Diet: It feeds mainly on fruits but will also eat leaves, flowers, bark, or termites during the dry season when food is scarce.
A_Crisis: The brown spider monkey is one of the species enrolled in the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria Ex-Situ Programme. It is currently classified as Critically Endangered (CR) by the IUCN, and the size of their population in the wild is unknown. Ex-situ (captive) populations worldwide number less than 200 animals, so more conservation organizations need to join its population management program. This will increase the ex-situ population, which will serve as backup for future re-introductions into the wild.

A_Distribution: From Nepal to southern and eastern China, Indochina Peninsula, Hainan Island, and Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Mountainous forests near rivers between low and middle elevations.
A_Feature:
1. It has a pointed muzzle, a slender body, and a trunk that is slightly larger in the middle. It has distinctive white stripes that run from the sides of its head to its shoulders.
2. Its limbs are short and the toes are webbed. There is a stink gland near its anus that emits a special odor.
3. Its fur is long, coarse and fluffy, making the animal look like it is wearing a straw cape.
A_Behavior:
1. It is very vigilant and shy, which means it is rarely sighted in the wild. Its droppings are shaped like short rods and contain large amounts of crustacean or insect pieces.
Its droppings are often left near rivers and are easy to find. 
3. It requires environments with high water quality, so it is considered to be an indicator species.
4. It is a superb swimmer and diver, and mainly lives in forests near rivers. Its den can be a rock cave or a hole that it excavated. It is primarily active at dawn or dusk and usually follows a fixed routine. The species is generally solitary, so if two or more individuals are seen together, it is usually a female with her young.
A_Diet: Vertebrates such as rodents, snakes, frogs and fish, as well as invertebrates such as freshwater crabs and shrimps, snails, and large insects. Its diet is mostly crustaceans and insects.
A_Crisis: Destruction of river ecosystems, waterway pollution, animal traps, and feral dogs.

A_Distribution: The Talaud Islands off northern Sulawesi, Indonesia, inhabiting the canopy.
A_Feature: With their bill slightly longer than other parrots, their slim tongue has brush-like tips that help them feed on nectar and pollen.
A_Behavior: An endemic species in Indonesia, the male and female look similar in appearance.
A_Diet: Mainly feeding on nectar and pollen, they occasionally eat insects and fruits for supplement.
A_Crisis:
1.Loss of habitats.
2. The demand of pet trade.

A_Distribution: Mainly distributed in the Amazon region in South America, tropical savanna, and the rainforest periphery in the Amazon region.
A_Habitat: Mostly in the forest areas with higher humidity.
A_Feature:
1.The skin of the head and limbs is black with yellow to orange scales on top and around the eye and ear.
2.An adult male tortoise can reach 50cm in length, while females are slightly smaller, measuring 25 cm.
A_Behavior:
1.Breeding season coincide with the rainy season, which is from July to September. Though not apparently territorial, rival males battle during courtship and copulation.
2. 4-8 eggs in a clutch, which takes 150-180 days to hatch.
A_Diet: Being omnivorous, they feed on fruits, flowers, grass, carrion, and small invertebrates.

A_Distribution: Its distribution in South America  ranges from Venezuela and the Guianas, south to Brazil, west to the upstream areas of the Amazon River in Ecuador and Peru.
A_Habitat: Tropical forest
A_Feature:
1. They have two curved claws on the fore limbs, three on the hind, which they use to hang from the tree.
2. They have two layers of fur, the underfur is softer, and the overhair rougher. During dry seasons, it is brown. In the rainy seasons, the hair is tinged with green, due to the algae growing on the hair. 
3. They have neither incisors nor real canine teeth. With their hardened lips, they can cut leaves off.
4. They do not hibernate, although their metabolism is really slow.
A_Behavior:
1.With their limbs and claws, they hang upside down from trees, and inch along by pulling hand-over-hand. They sit on the fork of trees at times, but with their claws hooked on the branch.
2. Being nocturnal, they forage at night and hang curled-up during the day when sleeping.
3. Strong swimmers, they cannot walk or stand. Being placed on the ground, they would try to grasp hold a target with their claws and pull themselves forward.
4. They can defend with their long arms and sharp claws, whipping on the intruder, potentially causing deep cuts. They can also bite with their teeth.
A_Diet: They feed on leaves, sprouts, and fruits.

A_Distribution: North-western part of Colombia, South America
A_Habitat: Tropical forests or secondary forests.
A_Feature: Bare-faced, with all exposed skin black, They have a shock of white hair on top of their head. Their back and tail are black while the belly is white.
A_Behavior:
1. The Cotton-top Tamarin is a diurnal species inhabiting tropical forests, open woods, or secondary forests. They are arboreal and they even sleep in the tree at night.
2. They usually appear in groups, with approximately 3-9 individuals in a group.
A_Diet: Being omnivorous, They feed on fruits, sprouts, insects, spiders, bird eggs, and small vertebrates.
A_Crisis:
1. Habitat destruction.
2. Illegal capture for pet trade.

A_Distribution: Peru, Bolivia, and Brazil, South America.
A_Feature:
1. Azara’s Night Monkeys have large, beautiful eyes. Usually seen at dusk, they have such an out-of-the-world night vision that they can accurately catch a flying insect in the dark forest. 
2. They often leap from trees to trees along the vines, looking for food. They are able to make exceptionally long leaps.
A_Behavior: Azara's night monkeys are monogamous species that form nuclear families, with the male remaining present to raise the young. Often seen moving around with their children on their back, they are no doubt a sweet sight to see, showing how close their family members are.
A_Diet: Being omnivorous, they feed on fruits, insects, vertebrates, and eggs.

A_Distribution: Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, and southern China.
A_Feature:
1. Similar to Slow Loris in appearance.
2. Smaller in size, they have a very short tail, hidden beneath the fur. With large eyes and round head, they have a white stripe extending from the nose to the forehead, medium-sized ears, reddish-brown fur on their back, a ventral part that is greyish-white, and limbs tinged with silver-grey coloration.
3. They have a claw on the second toe of each leg, with nails on the rest of the toes. The second digit of their forelimb is shorter than the other ones. Individuals from China have a brown stripe stretching from their nape and tapers down along the spine until it obscures on the waist. The skin of their ears, nose, hand and legs is dark.
A_Behavior:
1. With the opposable thumbs, their hands and feet have strong grasp, allowing them to stay in the tree for a long period.
2. Individuals in the wild, due to the consumed food, produce a toxic secretion under their arms. They also lick the gland to poison their teeth, so that they can fend themselves when being threatened. Under captive environment, however, the brachial gland is no longer toxic since the consumed food is different.
3. They move very slowly, hence the name.
A_Diet: Being omnivorous, they feed on fruits, insects, bird eggs, and small birds.
A_Crisis: Lesser Slow Loris are being caught, traded as pets. Moreover, their habitats have been devastated due to the unsettling political situation and the perturbation of war. Their population decline, therefore, is worrying.

A_Distribution: Along the southwest coast of Madagascar
A_Habitat: Dry deciduous forests, or brushwoods.
A_Feature:
1. Small mammals, they measure 40-50 cm in length, with the tail reaching 20-27 cm.
2. They weigh between 120-270 grams, depending on the seasons.
3. Their fur is soft and their eyes are lustrous and are surrounded by dark rings.
A_Behavior:
1. The only known primate to hibernate, they store the energy as fat in their tails, which serves as their energy source during torpor. 
2. The hibernation can last up to 6 months, during which they curl up tightly into a ball shape. Their body temperature vary with the surrounding as they gradually consume the fat, awaiting the next wet season.
A_Diet: They are omnivorous and feed on fruits, seeds, leaves, and insects.

A_Distribution: West part of Colombia, Meso-America
A_Habitat: Warm, humid tropical  rainforest
A_Feature:
1. They come in diverse colors, mint-green, yellow, orange, at times even white, but yellow and dark yellow individuals are most commonly seen, hence the name.
2. They measure 47 cm in average, with females slightly bigger, about 50-55 cm.
A_Behavior:
1. Many kinds of Poison-dart frogs lay their spawn in the water-filled base of bromeliad leaves or tree hole. They are often hidden under leaf litter, or even lay eggs there.
2. Colorful small frogs, most poison-dart frog feature their bright color, which serves as a warning coloration to their predators. They are so named because the indigenous people in South America applied their toxin on the tip of darts in their hunt. 
3. Their poison comes from their prey, such as insects and spiders, and through bioaccumulation, the toxin is stored in the glands in their skin, as self-defense mechanism. In captivity, however, individuals are not fed with poisonous food, and the venomity usually disappear in about 6 months.
A_Diet: They feed on insects or spiders.

A_Distribution: Meso-America, Brazil, Colombia, southern Venezuela, and the Guianas
A_Habitat: Warm, humid tropical  rainforest
A_Feature:
1. They are named for their distinctly bright yellow coloration and varying black stripes. The broad black bands break off as they age, gradually into black spots.
2. Their average length is about 30-40 cm.
A_Behavior:
1. Many kinds of Poison-dart frogs lay their spawn in the water-filled base of bromeliad leaves or tree hole. They are often hidden under leaf litter, or even lay eggs there.

A_Habitat: Warm, humid tropical  rainforest
A_Feature:
1. They are prominently green or light blue, with black bands or spots on them.
2. They measure averagely about 30-40 cm in length.
A_Behavior:
1. Many kinds of Poison-dart frogs lay their spawn in the water-filled base of bromeliad leaves or tree hole. They are often hidden under leaf litter, or even lay eggs there.

A_Distribution: Southern Suriname, South America
A_Habitat: Warm, humid tropical  rainforest
A_Feature:
1. Prominently blue, they are covered with black spots.
2. They average approximately 30-40 cm in length.
A_Behavior:
1. Many kinds of Poison-dart frogs lay their spawn in the water-filled base of bromeliad leaves or tree hole. They are often hidden under leaf litter, or even lay eggs there.

A_Distribution: The Amazon River regions in Brazil, The Guianas, Peru, South America
A_Feature:
1. They are the largest fresh-water fish in the Amazon River.
2. They can live up to 60 years old, but aren't mature enough to reproduce until 30 years old.
3. Their scales are uniquely structured and layered so as to fend off piranha attacks.
A_Behavior: They breathe with their gill, but have a lung-like swim bladder. They often swim leisurely near the surface, and breathe the air above the water with gulps. When the water is under-oxygenated, they would surface for the air. During dry seasons, they can also survive in the mud.
A_Diet: They are omnivorous and feed more carnivorously on fish, frogs, insects, and birds.

A_Distribution: The Amazon River region in South America.
A_Habitat: The surface layer of the river.
A_Feature:
1. In its prime, a Pink-tailed chalceus is pink, with the dorsal side golden-olive green, and the ventral side silver.
2. They feature their large iridescent scales that taper off toward the underside, especially so on the lateral line. With rather short head, and a protruding upper lip, they can reach 24.5 cm in length.
A_Behavior:
1. As a predator in the upper layer of the river, they feed on worms, insects and smaller fish.
2. They live in highly oxygenated waters.
A_Diet: They are carnivorous.

A_Distribution: Amazon River and Orinoco River area, South America
A_Habitat: Mid-layer of the river
A_Feature: Prominently dark, but the ventral part, the chin, and the pectoral fin are red, as well as parts of the pelvic fin.
A_Behavior:
1. Often mistaken as Piranha, they are actually omnivores that mainly feed on fruits.
2. They crush seeds and nuts with their molariform teeth.
3. During flooding season, they enter the inundated area, where they eat the seeds and help distribute them.
A_Diet: They feed on seeds, crustaceans, and small fishes.

A_Distribution: The Amazon River region in South America
A_Habitat: Upper layer of the river.
A_Feature:
1. Band-shaped and the mouth opening downward, they have pouch-like jaw, which closes upward. The male carry the eggs, larvae or early juveniles with it.
2. With a pair of barbels and large eyes, their scales are conspicuously large, edged with powder-pink shades, which fades with age.
3.Their anal fin extends to the caudal fin, with the dorsal fin shorter than the anal fin. They can measure up to 120 cm in length
A_Behavior: They can jump out of water surface to capture their prey.
A_Diet: Fish, shrimps, ad worms

A_Feature: They measure up to 1.5 meters and weigh 70 kg.
A_Behavior: They are migratory fish. During dry season, they go upstream for breeding. The alevins then head downstream in the rainy season, into the flooded area, where food abounds.
A_Diet: They are omnivorous.
A_Crisis:
1. They are suffering from over-fishing in recent years.
2. They are also inflicted by water pollution caused by deforestation and industrial development.
3. Their population has been most threatened by the construction of the water dam, which makes it impossible for the fish to swim upstream for breeding.

A_Distribution: Tabajos River, one of the tributaries of Amazon River, South America
A_Habitat: Bottom layer of the water
A_Feature:
1.They have a rounded pectoral fin, which connects to their body into a disc shape. The juveniles lighter-colored on their back, and turn dark after they reach 20-30 cm in diameter.
2. The golden patterns on the back resemble donuts or the number "8".
3. The posterior is a slender stinging spine, on which there are small dorsal fins and scythe-like caudal fins. Toward halfway or two-third down the tail, there is a barbed sting, with venom gland and venom sac underneath. It is highly poisonous. The barbs are shed 2-3 times a year.
A_Behavior:
1. Males have a pair of specialized, baculate claspers at the base of their tail, while on females they appear separated and fan-like.
2. They often lie on the silt floor, sometimes dive into the mud. They are carnivorous and feed on small fish, shrimps, crabs, and other demersal invertebrates.
A_Diet: Fish, crustaceans, and insects.

A_Distribution: The Amazon River
A_Habitat: Bottom layer of the water
A_Feature:
1.Laterally-compressed, they have a relatively pointed snout.
2. Mature individuals have metallic spots on their flanks, and extended rays on their dorsal, anal, and caudal fins.
A_Behavior: Before breeding, they clear up the sand on the substrate, and the eggs are laid on the river bed. They are facultative mouth-brooders.
A_Diet: They are omnivorous.

A_Distribution: They originate from the Amazon River, South America.
A_Feature: Resembling Largemouth black bass in appearance, they form salient humps on their forehead.
A_Behavior: The rainy season is their breeding season. Due to their discreet nature, they prefer to lay eggs on submerged branches.
A_Diet: They are carnivorous.

A_Distribution: South America
A_Feature:
1. Their body is elongated, oval shape, laterally-flattened, with a short tail. They have comparatively large head in proportion with the tail. Their eyes are near the upper part of the head.
2. With a pointed mouth on the snout, whose opening doesn't reach their eyes. Their lateral line is seen where the anal fin starts. There are upper and lower lateral lines.
3. Over-all greyish green, they can change their color depending on the environment.
A_Behavior:
1. As a euryhaline fish, they live mostly in downstream rivers, or littoral lagoons, with their physical traits varying according to the environment.
2. When the fry hatch, the parents keep taking care of the young, but they lack the mouth brooder as the shelter for the young.
A_Diet: They are omnivorous.

A_Distribution: Southeast part of China, Hainan Island, Indochina Peninsula, and the Malay Archipelago.
A_Habitat: Open forests or forest edge, bamboo forests, and open grass slopes
A_Feature: Prominently verdant green, with a blue tail and marron-adorned throat, the blue-tailed bee-eater appears especially fascinating with their glamorous looks and sonorant calls, decorating the summertime sky of Kinmen. Therefore, they are called the Summer Fairies by the locals.
A_Behavior:
1. They are renowned summer migratory birds, which migrate to southeast China and Hainan islands to breed around the time of Tomb-sweeping Festival, and head southward in winter.
2. They are excellent at eating flying insects.
3. They roost at night in aggregation. They aggregate toward their night roosting site at dusk. In Kinmen, these sites include Agricultural Research Institute, and the woods near Golden Turtle Mountain and Hosha
A_Diet: They feed on insects such as bees, butterflies, and dragonflies…etc.

A_Distribution: Malaysia, Sumatra, and Borneo
A_Feature:
1. Males can reach 200 cm in length, weighing up to 2 kg; females about 75 cm and 1.6 kg of weight.
2. Both male and female have blue skin on their face, while male individuals have an apparent crest.
A_Behavior:
1. They like to act alone, and usually forage at the bottom of the forest at dawn or dusk. They are territorial too. 
2. To attract females during breeding seasons, the male spread their wings into two fans, displaying the ocelli (eyes) on the secondaries, and dance in front of the female. Hence the name, " pheasant with a hundred eyes".
3. They are monogamous birds.
A_Diet: They feed on fruits, seeds, leaf sprouts, and invertebrates, …etc.
A_Crisis: Due to damage to the Asian rainforest, where the Great argus inhabit, it is listed as vulnerable by IUCN.

A_Distribution: Parts of Madagascar
A_Habitat: They live in primary forests, secondary rainforests, deciduous forests, and forest plantation, sometimes in brushwoods or mangroves.
A_Feature:
1. An Aye-aye has a long, bushy tail, its body covered with tousled, coarse hair. Adults are dark brown or black,  with sparse white hair. 
2. They are characterized by their yellowish-orange, or sandy brown eyes, surrounded by dark rings, large and triangular-shaped ears, and pinkish, short nose.
3. There is no apparent difference between male and female. Their incisors are large and ever-growing.
A_Behavior:
1. They are nocturnal, solitary species and spend most time in the canopy. They rub their neck, cheeks and rump regions against the tree to mark their scent.
2. They have the most intriguing method to forage. They tap on the branches or bamboos, producing echo sounds, by which they find out where the grubs are, before gnawing a hole and scooping out the grubs with their elongated middle fingers.
A_Diet: They are omnivorous and feed on leaves, fruits, nectar, and insects.
A_Crisis:
1. They face extinction due to the rapid loss of natural habitats.
2. They are hunted by the locals for the superstition, which deems them as bad omens or harbingers of evil.

A_Distribution: Southern Part of Madagascar, Africa.
A_Habitat: Dry areas
A_Feature:
1. They are named for the yellow lines radiating from the center of each plate on the carapace. The patterns vary from individual to individual.
2.Hatchlings have yellow spots, instead of radiating lines, on their carapace, and eventually develop radiating lines as they grow.
3.Their carapace can measure up to 40 cm in length.
A_Behavior: 8-10 eggs in each clutch, which takes about 3 months to hatch.
A_Diet: As herbivores, they feed on fruits and grass.
A_Crisis:
1.They are facing extinction due to the rapid loss of natural habitats.
2. They are also being hunted owing to the need of local people for protein.
3. They are being caught and traded out of the demand for pets.

A_Distribution: Northern areas of South America, including Panama, Colombia, Paraguay, Venezuela, Guyana, Brazil, northern Argentina, and a few Caribbean islands.
A_Habitat: Mainly from forest periphery to plains.
A_Feature:
1.They have dark or black carapaces, generally an elongated oval with sides that are nearly parallel, although the sides of males may curve inwards.
2. Their limbs and cheeks show bright, red spots.
3. Limbs are usually cylindrical, with 5 claws on the fore limbs and 4 on the hind, but no visible toes.
A_Behavior:
1. They are diurnal.
2. The breeding season for females in the wild is July to September. In captivity, however, they can breed all year round.
3. Their wide range of diet and long-distance migrating behavior make them significant distributors of the seeds of tropical plants.
A_Diet: Being omnivorous, they feed on fruits, flowers, grass, carrion, and small invertebrates.

A_Distribution: Yunnan in China, Myanmar, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and northern Sumatra.
A_Habitat: The dense canopy of tropical rainforests on lowlands or mountain slopes, or tress over 30 meters tall.
A_Feature:
1.White-handed gibbons are dichromatic in pelage, from gray to black to brown or  light cream color to light brown. The hairless and black face is surrounded by a ring of short white fur.The fur of hands and feet are both white.
2. Its' long arms reach below the knees when it is standing.
A_Behavior:
1. The white-handed gibbon lives in family groups consisting of a pair of adults and their offspring. Each family lives within a fixed territory, and they are very territorial. Loud calls are used to assert ownership of territories and drive off intruders.
2. It is an arboreal animal that frequently swings through the trees with its long arms, and can move forward up to 3 m with each swing.
3. Its long arms get in the way when it is walking on the ground, so it will hop sideways with its arms held high. It cannot swim and, so is afraid of water.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, mainly diet  on fruits,  leaves, few insects, eggs, and small invertebrates.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss, habitat fragmentation, and poaching.

A_Distribution: Forests and wetlands on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo.
A_Habitat: Native to tropical regions such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Sumatra, and Borneo.
A_Feature: A large crocodile species with a long and elongated snout containing 76 to 84 sharp, pointed teeth. The eyes and nostrils are located on the top of the head. It has a streamlined body and a muscular tail. The body is olive-green with faint black stripes across the back. Most juveniles are dark brown.
A_Behavior:
1. Mature females can grow up to 2.5 to 3 meters in length, while males are about 5 meters long.
2. Sexual maturity is reached at around 20 years of age. In the wild, breeding season coincides with the local wet season, which generally lasts from November to February or April to June each year. Female crocodiles will build nests out of dead leaves, twigs, and pieces of wood at the base of large trees near the water.
A_Diet: Carnivorous. Diet includes birds, mammals, reptiles, fish, insects, and crustaceans.
A_Crisis: Threatened by human activities such as hunting, logging, fishing, and the excessive use of aquatic resources. They are often used for making for handicrafts and beads.

A_Distribution: From southern India, the Malay Peninsula, to the coastal regions of southern China,  Sumatra and Borneo.
A_Habitat: Freshwater wetlands, lakes, downstream delta floodplains, and mangroves.
A_Feature:
1. It is the smallest of all otter species. Its head and trunk are elongated and streamlined, while its limbs and claws are short with webbing between the toes. Its fur is short and dense.
2. Most of its body is covered with dark, brown fur, except for the face and the neck, which are of a pale, cream color. A layer of very fine, soft inner fur keeps its body dry and warm.
A_Behavior:
1. It is a social animal that lives in groups and communicates vocally.
2. It is active at dawn and dusk. It swims with its ears flat against the head and its forelimbs held close to its belly. Its round nose helps reduce water resistance. It is a master diver and swimmer. It often hunts underwater but must still surface to breathe. Its dexterous forelimbs are used to catch prey or to turn over rocks in search of food."
A_Diet: Invertebrates, crustaceans, fish and amphibians in the water, as well as aquatic fowls and rodents near the water.
A_Crisis: Loss of habitat, waterway pollution,  poaching

A_Distribution: The Andes Mountain range in South America, up to 4,800 meters above sea level, and are kept by people in southern Peru and western Bolivia.
A_Feature: Adult males are measured 90 to 100 centimeters tall at the shoulders and 200 centimeters in length, and weigh between 70 to 90 kg. They look like sheep with a long neck.
A_Behavior:
1. Special hemoglobin in its blood ensures that it gets enough oxygen from the thin air of high mountains.
2. It is a social species. A wild herd is usually led by a male and includes several females and their young. The male llama watches over the group and makes a warning call when it detects danger. Llamas communicate through posture and soft grunts. They are easy to care for in captivity.
3. Llamas may look docile, but they actually have a strong personality. They will puff up their cheeks and spit when in conflict or fight over food. They sidekick with their rear legs if they are startled or when they do not want to be touched.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.

A_Distribution: The tropical parts of South America, stretching from Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador to Uruguay to northern Argentina. They have also been found on mountain ridges below an elevation of 2,500 meters on both the eastern and western sides of the Andes Mountains.
A_Feature:
1. Its upper body is brown or grey, with a white abdomen. Its slender, brown-black tail is 32 to 69 centimeters long, covered with yellow bands and is used for balancing. Its claws and forelimbs are strong enough for climbing and for digging out food from rotting logs.
2. The coati has a narrow head, and their long, slightly upturned nose is very dexterous.
A_Behavior:
1. It turns over leaf litter and gravel in search of food. It is a great climber and swimmer, and can also rotate the joints on its limbs and its ankles to climb down from trees head-first.
 2. Females usually stay close to their birthplace, while males move further to other places and form groups of around 30 with unrelated females.
 3. It is a diurnal animal that is mostly arboreal and spends most of its time foraging. It may sometimes damage crops, but otherwise play an important role in pest control. It also helps with the dispersion of certain seeds.
 4. It rubs its neck and lower abdomen against specific locations to leave a scent from its anal glands. The scent is its claim to the territory.
A_Diet: It is omnivorous and feeds mainly on fruits and invertebrates, including palm trees, eggs, beetle larvae, scorpions, centipedes, spiders, ants, termites, lizards, small mammals, and rodents.

A_Distribution: Wild populations are found in southern Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia and the Arab Peninsula of Africa. Domesticated donkeys can be found worldwide.
A_Feature: It is physically smaller than a zebra but has a bigger head and longer ears. Its back is usually grey but takes on a red tint in summer. Its belly is white. Some have a dark stripe that runs along the back. Its erect mane is long and thin. Its tail has a tufted tip. The hooves are long and narrow.
A_Behavior:
1. Both wild and feral donkeys are diurnal animals. They have a social structure similar to that of horses, with solitary males, reproductive herds, and bachelor or juvenile herds.
 2. Its long and narrow hooves help it balance on uneven, rocky grounds.
 3. Donkeys travel slower, but can drink less frequently than horses. They don't require much water and can continously work in the hot weather, or even when there is not enough food. They are usually cheaper than horses, which is why they continue to be an important animal people use to transport cargo.
 4. Domesticated donkeys naturally guard their young, so they are often trained to protect livestock such as sheep and goats. They will attack enemies without hesitation, even if the threat is a large dog or a human.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.

A_Distribution: Europe, etc.
A_Feature:
1. Ponies are essentially small horses. It is between 100 to 150 centimeters tall and is less than 86 centimeters when measured from the ground up to the shoulders.
 2. Ponies come in a wide variety of colors. It has an over-sized head, thicker legs, flowing mane as well as a "forelock" on its head that look like bangs.
A_Behavior: Ponies can be temperamental, and might kick or bite their owner or bystanders unless they have been professionally trained. They do not ruminate.
A_Diet: It is herbivorous and eats mainly grass but will also eat tender tree leaves.

A_Distribution: Between 3,000 and 5,000 meters above sea level in the Andes Mountain range in northern Chile.
A_Feature: It sits on its behind and holds food in its paws to eat. Its habitat has very little water, but dew drops on the grass that it consumes is enough for survival.
A_Behavior:
1. Chinchilla resembles a squirrel. Around 60 hairs grow from each follicle, so its fur is especially soft. It likes to take sand baths with volcanic ash to remove oil from their sebaceous glands.
2. It usually emerges after sunset from rocky crevices or caves to hop and climb with great agility across the rocky terrain. The chinchilla population has declined drastically due to poaching by humans for their pelts.
3. It is a nocturnal and social but territorial animal that feeds mainly on licorice. Its habitat is usually barren, so it will also eat any plants that it can find.
A_Diet: It is herbivorous and is fed mixed grains and fruits in captivity but will eat any kind of plant that grows on rocky, barren soil.

A_Distribution: The Kalahari Desert of South Africa, Namibia, and southwestern Angola.
A_Feature: It’s  measured between 25 to 35 centimeters in length and has a long, slender tail. There are black spots to its eye sockets, making it seem as if the animal is wearing a pair of sunglasses. Its ears are small and round, and can be closed when digging so as to keep sand out of Its ear canals. It uses its long and curved claws for digging tunnels and hunting.
A_Behavior:
1. Desert nights are freezing cold, so the first thing a meerkat does in the morning when it wakes up is to use the black parts of its belly to absorb the sun’s heat to warm up its entire body.
2. It lives in groups of around thirty. They dig holes in the ground as their dens and live together in a large tunnel system.
3. If a group of meerkats is outside eating, at least one will be on sentry duty. The meerkat on the lookout will make a warning call when it detects danger.
4. The females and males will split their duties during the breeding season, with the females suckling and the males on guard.
A_Diet: It is carnivorous and feeds mainly on arthropods, reptiles, small mammals and eggs.

A_Distribution: A small-eared pig species originally found in Lanyu. It originated from wild boars domesticated by the Tao people.
A_Feature: The Lanyu pig has a square trunk. It is relatively small with thick, short and strong limbs. Its fur is black and glossy. Its ears are small and erect. Bristles grow from its neck to its back. The middle of its back is slightly dented. A mature Lanyu pig weighs on average no more than 80 kilograms.
A_Behavior: It is a kind of domesticated pigs and is soft-tempered compared to wild boars. Its small size means that it could be carried when its human owners are migrating. It is well adapted to humid, subtropical climates.
A_Diet: It is omnivorous. In the wild, it feeds mainly on plants such as tender leaves, roots, berries and crops. It also sometimes eats invertebrates such as insects and worms.

A_Distribution: Southern Canada, the United States, and the northern parts of South America.
A_Feature: Its fur is greyish-black, and there are 5 to 10 black bands on its tail. It also has black markings that form something that resembles a mask on its face. Its snout is quite sharp. Its toes are unwebbed, and the claws are not retractable. The five digits on each of its forelimbs are separated, and its footprint is similar to that of a human's. Females have four pairs of mammary glands.
A_Behavior:
1. It usually lives near water sources in dense forests or bushes. It is a nocturnal animal that is good at climbing trees and swimming.
 2. Racoons do not hibernate and are active all-year-round in warmer regions. In colder areas, they will overwinter inside caves and emerge when the weather is warm. Their body temperature remains the same, and their metabolism does not slow down during winter. They rely on their body fat to survive the winter, and their body weight may drop by half by the end of winter.
 3. Racoons have very acute senses of smell and touch. They usually use their forepaws to feel for food in shallow water and then put it in their mouths, hence their reputation for “washing” their food.
A_Diet: It is omnivorous and eats crustaceans such as shrimps and crabs, as well as frogs, fish, nuts, seeds, acorns and berries.

A_Distribution: From southern Mexico to Brazil.
A_Habitat: Tropical forests
A_Feature:
1. It weighs between 1.84 and 4.6 kilograms. Its body length is 41 to 57 centimeters. Its tail is as long as its body.
2. The kinkajou is related to the racoon but looks more like a monkey. It is one of the few carnivores with a prehensile tail that can act as a fifth hand. It uses its long tail to jump between branches or to hide its young.
A_Behavior:
1. Nocturnal animal.
2. Its long tongue is used for licking honey.
3. This adept climber uses its tail, feet and claws to clamber between branches. The naked parts of its body have scent glands that can be rubbed against trees to communicate with others of its kind.
A_Diet: It is omnivorous. It is particularly fond of honey and fruit, a trait that is unusual among carnivores.

A_Distribution: Found inwestern half of Taiwan, eastern India, Nepal, northern Vietnam, and southern China.
A_Habitat: Taipei Grass Frog inhabits swamps where emerged plants grow extensively.
A_Feature: Taipei Grass Frog is small-sized which has a slender body with SVL from 3-5 cm. This species bears golden iris, green body, and white dorsolateral folds. A dark stripe runs along the dorsolateral glandular fold on either side.
A_Behavior: Taipei Grass Frogs are nocturnal. The coming of the plum rain season each year marks the start of their breeding season. Male frogs have a tiny mating call. They start with single sound “Chee” and then progress to continuous noise “Chee Chou”, just like the sound of glass being wiped. In fall, Taipei Grass Frogs move out of the water and live onshore; therefore, protecting  the terrestrial buffer zone around ponds plays an important part of the effort to conserve the habitat of this species.
A_Diet: Diet consists mainly of small arthropods.
A_Crisis: Taipei Grass Frog is threaten by the reduction of waters where they inhabit, as well as the pollution of their habitats that caused by conventional agricultural techniques

A_Distribution: Swinhoe’s Frog is endemic to Taiwan. It lives near the rivers and streams in low- and mid- altitude mountains.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting aquatic environments such as rivers and streams.
A_Feature: The body is slender and flattened. The dorsolateral folds are indistinct. The skin is smooth; there are distinctive wart-like bumps on the side of body. The limbs are slender. The finger and toe tips are formed into discs. There is a yellowish-white longitudinal stripe on the upper lip. The dorsum is green or yellowish-brown, occationally speckled with dark brown spots. The ventrum is white.
A_Behavior: Swinhoe’s Frog ususally makes mating calls in streams. It makes a chirping noise that is often mistaken for bird calls.
A_Diet: Diet consists mainly of small arthropods.

A_Distribution: Taiwan and southern China.
A_Habitat: Stillwater ponds and swampy wetlands.
A_Feature: Olive Frogs have stout body. The body color is brown, with an indistinct mid-dorsal stripe on the center of dorsum.
A_Behavior: Olive Frogs are common in urban areas. They can often be found calling in artificial waters in spring and summer. They have a distinct call that sounds like “Ge, Ge, Ge.”
A_Diet: Diet consists mainly of small arthropods.

A_Distribution: From East Asia to Southeast Asia.
A_Habitat: Extensively distributed in most kinds of environments , from lowlands to low-altitude moutains. Capable of surviving in highly developed urban environments as well.
A_Feature: Asian Spined Toads have coarse skin and can be identified by the black pattern around the eyes and snout.
A_Behavior: Asian Spined Toads are common from plains to low-altitude mountains. Urbanized populations have emerged in recent years. During the breeding season in spring and summer, they can often be found in park ponds and gutters, making  continuous “Croak Croak Croak” calls.
A_Diet: Diet consists mainly of small arthropods.

A_Distribution: Found throughout East and Southeast Asia.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting aquatic environments such as streams and ponds.
A_Feature: Yellow Pond Turtle has rounded head and egg-shaped  carapace that runs an indistinct central keel. The top of its head is olive colored. There is a wide, yellow longitudinal stripe behind the eyes. The carapace is grayish-brown or yellowish-brown in color. The plastron is a yellow or brown color, with large black spots on the outer margin of each plate. The plastron of males is distinctly concave.
A_Behavior: Yellow Pond Turtles generally inhabit waters such as streams or river valleys near hills. They usually bury themselves in the mud under the water with only the head exposed to observe the surroundings. They will only emerge and be in action if the coast is clear.
A_Diet: Omnivorous. Feed on worms, insects, shrimps, crabs, fish, river snails, as well as plant stems, leaves, and seeds.
A_Crisis: Owing to the trade of Asian turtles, wild individuals are at high risk of poaching.

A_Distribution: Found in Taiwan, Vietnam, and southern China.
A_Habitat: Chinese Cobra inhabits wild or cultivated areas from the lowlands to low-altitudes mountains.
A_Feature: Chinese Cobra has a U-shaped white band on the back of its neck.
A_Behavior: In Taiwan, Chinese Cobras can be found from lowlands to low-altitude mountains. Some populations at once withdraw to the rural regions owing to human activity, but they are now showing signs of adapting to urban life by hiding in abandoned parts of the city. However, as long as there is urban development, Chinese Cobras are forced to flee and scatter. Consequently, the misconception that the snakes are liberated and alien species is usually spreading on the Internet. Cobras play an important role in controlling rodent populations and maintaining ecological balance. Most people shy away from them out of ignorance and fear, but in reality, it is the Chinese Cobras that avoid humans like the plague.
A_Diet: Chinese Cobras feed mainly on small mammals.
A_Crisis: Threatened by habitat exploitation and human attack.

A_Distribution: Haiti and the Dominican Republic
A_Habitat: Inhabiting reef rocks  around islands.
A_Feature: The Rhinoceros Iguana is heavily built and has a grayish-blue color. Their name is derived from the horn protruding on their forehead that give them a rhino-like appearance.
A_Behavior: The Rhinoceros Iguana inhabits the islands in Central America. It has adapted to its environment by developing salt glands that excrete excess salt through its nasal cavity.
A_Diet: Omnivorous, with a preference for plants.
A_Crisis: Wild populations are threatened by poaching.

A_Distribution: Found throughout Southeast Asia. It is an invasive species in Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting forests an is  arboreal, but could also be found on the walls of buildings in urban areas.
A_Feature: The tokay gecko has a broad, large heand. The total length reaches about 25 cm. The body color is brown or bluish-gray. Numerous red spots are scattered over the surface of the body.
A_Behavior: Tokay Geckos are widely distributed throughout Southeast Asia.  In early years, this species served as a common ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine. The geckos were sold after being flattened and sun-dried. Individuals in escape have been caught throughout Taiwan. There have been stable populations established in Guishan, Kaohsiung in recent years. Tokay Geckos are quite fierce and bite powerfully. They prey on insects and other reptiles.
A_Diet: Tokay Geckos feed mainly on small arthropods and small reptiles.
A_Crisis: An invasive species that threatens the survival of native animals.

A_Distribution: Western Asia.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting desert environments.
A_Feature: The Tartari Sand Boa is quite small with a short, thick body. The labials is well-developed. The eyes are very tiny.
A_Behavior: The Tartari Sand Boa has well-developed labials that allows them to slither on the sands at speed. It is a nocturnal species.
A_Diet: Lizards and small mammals.

A_Distribution: Central Vietnam.
A_Habitat: Rivers and lakes at low altitudes.
A_Feature: The body and carapace of the Vietnamese Pond Turtle is dark brown. There are yellow stripes across the face.
A_Behavior: Vietnamese Pond Turtles have adapted to living in rivers and lakes. They were once widely distributed in Vietnam as they had few natural threats, but for a time were thought to be extinct in the wild due to over-hunting by humans. Although small populations have recently been rediscovered in the wild, they remain under heavy pressure from poaching.
A_Diet: Omnivorous with a preference for plants.
A_Crisis: The populations of this species are under serious threat from illegal poaching.

A_Distribution: Found in southwestern China amd northern Vietnam in Asia.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting aquatic environments such as ponds near rivers and streams.
A_Feature: The Chinese Crocodile Lizard is a species of lizard. It has a cylindrical body and a flattened tail like the crocodile. They usually measure between 32 to 36 cm long but can grow up to 40 cm. The body color of females tend to be yellowish-brown, while that of males tend to be reddish-brown.
A_Behavior: Chinese Crocodile Lizards are diurnal and are most active at dawn and dusk. As a semi-aquatic species, they can dive and stay down the water for a long time to escape predators if threatened. When the water temperature in its original habitat drops below 15.5°C between November and March, they will hibernate in rock crevices or tree holes. Chinese Crocodile Lizards are viviparous, and the gestation period is about 9 months, with 2 to 12 young born each time.
A_Diet: Chinese Crocodile Lizards feed on live amphibians, fish, earthworms, and insects.
A_Crisis: Poaching for the need from pet markets is continuing to reduce the number of wild individuals.

A_Distribution: Central-eastern Australia
A_Habitat: Living in deserts, as well as arid grasslands, scrublands, and woodlands.
A_Feature: The central bearded dragon is thick- and flattened bodied. Its head is wide and triangular. The ear openings are distinct. There are large, spiny scales behind the head, on the back of the neck, and on the throat. There are a row of regular conical spines running along the body sides.  The dorsum is yellowish-brown, yellow, or reddish-brown. There are two rows of irregular dark brown markings on the dorsum.
A_Behavior: Central bearded dragons are diurnal and terrestrial. They will inflate its head and body to intimidate predators.
A_Diet: Central bearded dragons are omnivorous and feed on insects and leafy plants.

A_Distribution: The southwestern  parts of North America (Oregon, America), south to the Baja Peninsula in Mexico.
A_Habitat: Living in deserts, grasslands, riverbeds, hills, scrublands, forests, wetlands and farmlands.
A_Feature: Total body length 1 to 1.5 m. Slender bodied and smooth scaled. The body colors and patterns vary widely. There are dark bands (black or brown) interlaced with light bands (white or yellow). Some individuals are striped . The ventrum is white and covered with black markings.
A_Behavior: The California King Snake is a member of the genus Lampropeltis. It often preys on venomous snakes in the wild, hence titled as "King Snake".
A_Diet: Mammals, reptiles, and amphibians.

A_Distribution: The eastern part of North America, from Michigan to eastern Texas, and eastern Mexico.
A_Habitat: Living in moist forests, grasslands, ranches, swamps, and alluvial plains.
A_Feature: Relatively small in size. The carapace is highly-domed. The plastron is large, with the pectorals and abdominals linked by a ligament which allows the tortoise to completely close its front and rear openings against predators. The carapace is dark brown, with yellow or orange radiating stripes and spots. The plastron is yellowish-brown in color.
A_Behavior: The Common Box Turtle is terrestrial and widely distriduted to various environments in North America. They are euryphagous and feed on a variety of foods.
A_Diet: Arthropods, annelids, mollusks, and plants.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss and roadkill.

A_Distribution: Xinjiang, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Pakistan, Iran, and Afghanistan.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting arid grasslands with low rainfall and loessal hills at the altitudes between 700 m and 1000 m.
A_Feature: The body is oval-shaped. The carapace is yellow, with large, black and concentric markings on the scutes. The plastron is khaki with large black markings on the scute. The four limbs are thick with four claws on each foot.
A_Behavior: Central Asian Tortoises are the species of the highest latitudes. They hibernate during winter and start breeding in early spring. Males will fight each other during the breeding season by retracting their heads and ramming their opponent with the front edge of their carapace.
A_Diet: Herbivorous. Central Asian Tortoises feed on  plant stems, succulent leaves, flowers, and fruit.

A_Distribution: East Africa and Southeast Africa
A_Habitat: Semi-arid grasslands.
A_Feature: The body is black with yellow spots. The dorsum is usually yellowish-brown while the ventrum is usually dark brown. The lower jaw and throat are yellow or pale yellow. Cylindrical bodied, short-headed, and large eyed. The tail is usually twice as long as the body. Despite its robustness, the legs are smaller than those of iguanas. There are hard scales on the head. A deep groove on each side runs along the entire body. The grooves provide  space for females to carry their eggs or for individuals full of foods to expand their body.
A_Behavior: The great plated lizards are diurnal. Although they are considered shy animals, males will sometimes fight over territory. They generally doesn’t bite when frightened. Their preferred survival mechanism is to use the plated tails for defense. When they are preyed upon, the lizards will run for a short distance and then stop still in a sudden; at the same time, they will also raise the tail to confuse the attacker and then squeeze the body into a crevice to escape.
A_Diet: Omnivorous.

A_Distribution: Found nearby the central and southern parts of India, Sri Lanka, and Pakistan.
A_Habitat: Primary habitats include arid grassland, scrublands, or abandoned farmlands. The home ranges are mostly in barren environments formed by the accumulation of dry clods of soil or leaf litter.
A_Feature: The shell is highly-domed, with radiating streaks that form star patterns. The supracaudals are not split. The body color is dark brown, and the spots, and stripes and the ventrum is yellow.  The limbs are club-like.
A_Behavior: Indian Star Tortoises are diurnal species that often wander in deserts to search for food. They prefer to inhabit arider environments.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.
A_Crisis: Due to overharvesting and habitat destruction, the wild populations decline sharply.

A_Distribution: Found throughout Asia in Taiwan, Vietnam, and southern China.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting the forest floor of low- and mid-altitude mountains and hills.
A_Feature: Hundred-Pace Viper is medium/large-sized snake with a thick, stout body. Its body length measures between 0.8 to 1.6 m. It has triangular head with upturned snout which is similar to a dead leaf. There are pit organs between the eyes and the nostrils. There are a row of triangular dark-brown markings on each side of the body. There are large, symmetric scales on the dark-brown head.
A_Behavior: Hundred-Pace Vipers are nocturnal or active at dawn and dusk. They are sit-and-wait predators, feeding mainly on frogs, toads, snakes, lizards, birds, and rodents,
A_Diet: Mammals, reptiles, amphibians, and birds.
A_Crisis: Taiwanese people usually kill snakes on sight owing to their fear and misunderstanding of venomous snakes, which  poses a threat to wild snakes.

A_Distribution: North America. From southern Canada, through the central US, to northeastern Mexico.
A_Habitat: Living in grasslands, scrublands, open forests, farmlands with soft, loose soil, as well as deserts.
A_Feature: Thick- and short-bodied, with pointy snout turning upwards. The body scales are quite coarse and keeled. The dorsum is pale brown, yellowish-brown or reddish-brown. There are three rows of dark brown markings running along the central line and the sides of the body. The ventrum is black and covered with small, earthy yellow spots. Total body length: 40 ~ 90 cm
A_Behavior: The Hognose Snake is a terrestrial species that is adept at digging and hiding in the sand. It makes a warning hiss when confronted by predators. If this fails to scare the enemy away, it will turn the belly up and play dead in order that the predator will lose interest.
A_Diet: It is adept at digging to hunt burrowing toads. It will also prey on other reptiles and occasionally small mammals or birds.

A_Distribution: From Southeast Asia to South Asia.
A_Habitat: Living in the forest floor and nearby rivers in tropical monsoon forests and evergreen forests at higher altitudes.
A_Feature: The largest tortoise in Asia. The carapace is broad and flattened, with the front and rear marginal scutes being saw-toothed. There are large scales on the front of the front legs and the back of the rear legs; those on the rear legs are particularly well-developed and protruding, hence it is also referred to as the “Six-legged Tortoise. The carapace is yellowish-brown or dark brown. The plastron is yellow, with the scute margin being dark brown.
A_Behavior: Asian Brown Tortoises are forest-dwelling and good climbers. Due to the lack of sunlight in the forest floor, they build nests out of plant litter for laying eggs during the breeding season, and use the heat generated by fermenting plant litter to incubate the eggs.
A_Diet: Omnivorous with a preference for plants.

A_Distribution: Found in the Aldabra Islands in the Indian Ocean.
A_Habitat: Living in grasslands, scrublands,  coastal mangrove swamps,  and beaches along the coasts.
A_Feature: Aldabra Giant Tortoises are among the largest tortoises in the world.
