Males are larger than females in size, with the carapace measuring between 90 ~ 130 cm and the body weighing between 230 ~ 300 kg on average. Female tortoises are smaller, with the carapace measuring around 90 cm and body weight reaching 159 kg on average. The body is generally deep grey or black, and the neck is very long .
A_Behavior: Aldabra Giant Tortoises have strong legs that allow them to travel over mountains and valleys in search of food in their original habitats. Their necks can be extended to reach leaves in higher places. During hot weather, they like to spend the entire day in the water.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.
A_Crisis: Stable populations now exist in the wild due to conservation efforts. The threat to its survival is decreasing.

A_Distribution: Central and South America, stretching from Mexico and the Letter Antilles to northern Argentina.
A_Habitat: Living in moist tropical rainforests and arid grasslands.
A_Feature: Thick-, muscular-bodied. Broad-, triangular-headed. Small-eyed amd vertical-irised. Smooth- and glossy-scaled. There is a dark brown stripe behind each eye. There are a variety of body patterns and colors. The back of the body is usually pale brown or grayish-red covered with large dark brown or reddish-brown saddle markings. The tail is more dark red.
A_Behavior: Common Boa Constrictors have a thick, muscular body. Juveniles are mostly arboreal, while adults spend most of their time on the ground. They are adept at ambushing their prey.
A_Diet: Mammals and birds.

A_Distribution: Found throughout East Asia including southern China, Taiwan, and southern Okinawa in Japan.
A_Habitat: Living in the moist forest floors or farmlands around the edge of forest in low-altitude mountains and hills.
A_Feature: Yellow-Margined Box Turtles have a rounded body form with highly-domed carapace, along the center of which runs a distinct keel. The pectorals and abdominals on the plastron are connected by tendons that allow the shell to be closed up. Olive-colored head, yellow cheeks, with a yellow longitudinal stripe extending from the rear of the eyes to the neck. The carapace is dark brown, while the central keel and the margin are yellow. The plastron is dark brown or black.
A_Behavior: Yellow-Margined Box Turtles are diurnal. They generally inhabit forests or bushes that are damp and near water, but rarely spend time in the water. The diet of Yellow-Margined Box Turtles consists mainly of plants and invertebrates. The provenance of its Chinese name “Snake-eating Turtle” is unknown.
A_Diet: Fruit, arthropods, annelids, and mollusks.
A_Crisis: Yellow-margined Box Turtles in Taiwan are gravely threatened by the trade of Asian turtles. Wild individuals are at high risk of poaching.

A_Distribution: Found in the Middle East including Yemen and southwest Saudi Arabia on the Arabian Peninsula.
A_Habitat: Living in humid lowlands, as well as the scrublands and woodlands in the mountains near the coasts.
A_Feature: The veiled chameleon has a flattened body with a helmet-like crest protruding from the top of the head. Males have a higher crest than females. There are prominent sawtooth-like scales raising along the middle line of the back and the abdomen . The body is mainly green, mosaicked with white, yellow, blue, and brown markings.
A_Behavior: Veiled chameleons were originally found in Yemen on the southern end of the Arabian Peninsula. It is a common reptile pet, but is also difficult to keep. In Taiwan, a veiled chameleon was first found by a tourist on Cijin beach in 2008. The invasive population became well known in 2013. These seemingly slender and sensitive animals are tough hunters in the wild and pose a serious threat to the survival of native lizards.
A_Diet: Arthropods, small reptiles, and small birds.
A_Crisis: An invasive species that threatens the survival of native animals.

A_Distribution: Central and South America, north from Panama, south to Argentina.
A_Habitat: Living in tropical rainforests, arid woodlands and grasslands.
A_Feature: The rainbow boa is mid- to large-sized snake with a thick, muscular body and thin, pointed head that is easily distinguishable from the neck. There are heat-sensing pits on the labials. All of the scales are smooth with a rainbow-like sheen. The back of the body is brown, orange-brown, or orange-red, covered with numerous dark brown circular markings. There are five thin, dark brown stripes on the head.
A_Behavior: Rainbow Boas tend to be nocturnal and like all members of the Boidae are viviparous snakes with 10 to 20 young born each time.
A_Diet: Reptiles, birds, and mammals.

A_Distribution: From the Balkans to the Caspian Sea in Central Asia.
A_Habitat: Dry and rocky hills, farmlands, and woods edge.
A_Feature: The total length is between 0.8 to 1.4 m. Legless lizards have ear openings and eyelids, while snakes do not.
A_Behavior: European Glass Lizards are diurnal and avid explorers of their surroundings. They have eyelids that can be closed when resting, which is a key character that distinguishes them from snakes.
A_Diet: European Glass Lizards are carnivorous and feed on arthropods, mollusks, reptiles, birds, eggs, and small mammals.

A_Distribution: The central and southern parts of Africa, west from Senegal, east to Uganda.
A_Habitat: Living in tropical rainforests, scrublands, savannas, and grasslands at low altitudes.
A_Feature: Stout-bodied, small- and slender-headed, and short-tailed. All of the scales are fine, smooth, and glossy. A wide black longitudinal band runs from the snout to the rear of the eyes. The back is black and covered with irregular pale brown markings.
A_Behavior: The Ball Python was named after the way it curls its body into a ball with the head hidden inside when disturbed and startled.
A_Diet: Small mammals.

A_Distribution: Southern Europe, northern Africa, eastern Africa, and  southwest Asia.
A_Habitat: Living in dry, sandy, and rocky environments.
A_Feature: A small to medium-sized lizard. The body is slender and somewhat cylindrical. The limbs are short, all with  five toes. The tail is about half as long as the body. This species is flat-headed, sharp- and flat- snouted, with eyelids. All of the scales are rounded, smooth, and glossy. The dorsum is brown and covered with many black spots. The ventrum is yellowish-white.
A_Behavior: Ocellated Skink
A_Diet: Arthropods, annelids, and mollusks.

A_Distribution: Taiwan, Vietnam, and southern China.
A_Habitat: Living in water bodies  on lowlands, such as ponds, swamps and slow-moving rivers.
A_Feature: Medium-sized. The carapace of juveniles have three raised keels while the side keels become indistinct in adults. There are yellow and green stripes alternated on the limbs and the sides of head and neck. The carapace is dark brown or dark olive-green; there are  light brown or orange-brown markings on the scutes. The plastron is yellowish-brown with black spots on each scute.
A_Behavior: Chinese Striped-neck Turtles are the most numerous, most widely distributed, and most common native species of freshwater turtle in Taiwan. They can often be found in rivers.
A_Diet: Plants, fish, and amphibians.
A_Crisis: Wild populations are under pressure from hunting.

A_Distribution: Endemic to Taiwan. Invasive populations have  emerged in Japan in recent years.
A_Habitat: Living in the edge of the forests at low- and mid-altitudes. It can be found in parks and schools.
A_Feature: Swinhoe’s Tree Lizard is endemic to Taiwan. It is the largest in size among the congeners in Taiwan. The dorsum is mostly brown. The edge of its mouth cavity is white or milky-white. There are protruding scales along the back of the neck. There are distinct white spots on the lower jaw of males. Male individuals have prominent dorsal crest and dewlap, as well as a distinct yellowish-green longitudinal stripe on each side of the body. Male lizards are highly territorial.
A_Behavior: Swinhoe’s Tree Lizards are diurnal. The males are highly territorial. They often inflate their throat and make push-up motions on the trunks to intimidate other individuals.
A_Diet: Invertebrates.

A_Distribution: The tropical rainforests on the Solomon Islands and Bougainville Islands in Oceania.
A_Habitat: The forest crown on  islands.
A_Feature: The Monkey-tailed Skin has a thick, strong body. It  is the largest skink in the world. The head is quite large and has a somewhat triangular shape.It has  blunt snout, powerful jaws, long and sharp claws on the limbs, and a strong and prehensile tail. The body is olive-green or brown with indistinct dark brown markings on the dorsum, while the ventrum is pale greenish-brown.
A_Behavior: Monkey-tailed Skinks are nocturnal species that are adept at climbing in tree  crowns in search of food. They are viviparous, with gestation period being 6 to 8 months. 1 to 2 young are born each time.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.

A_Distribution: Found throughout the western parts of North America.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting deserts, as well as arid prairies, scrublands, and woodlands.
A_Feature: The Gila Monster is stout bodied. It has a broad head, blunt snout, and small eyes. Its body is fat and  rounded, and its tail is thick and short. The back and limbs are covered with bead-like scales. The area between the snout and the corner of the mouth as well as the limbs are black. The top of the head, the body, and the tail are pink, orange, or orange-red, covered with irregular dark brown or black markings.
A_Behavior: Gila Monsters are diurnal. They are slow-moving and usually hide in rock burrows. They are very cling to the burrows they inhabit. Despite its slow movement, Gila Monsters are ale to bite powerfully. The poison it secretes is not fatal but will cause a lasting burning sensation in the wound.
A_Diet: Arthropods, reptiles, birds, bird eggs, and mammals.

A_Distribution: Found in southern China, Vietnam, Cambodia, and Thailand in Southeast Asia and East Asia. Inhabits broadleaf forests near rivers.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting river banks.
A_Feature: The Asian Water Dragon has a thick, strong body with a long, thin, and flattened tail. A row of spiny scales run along the back from the neck to the tail. The body is olive-green or yellowish-brown. The large scales on the throat and  lower lip are white. There are several dark brown bands on the tail.
A_Behavior: Asian Water Dragons are originally found in the southeastern areas of Asia. They live near waters and are adept swimmers and divers. Taiwan is not their natural habitat.The first Asian Water Dragon in Taiwan is recorded in Ankeng, New Taipei City, in 2011. The presence of this invasive species was attributed to intentional releases into the wild. Later, another introduced population was found in Linkou in New Taipei City. Asian Water Dragons are quite large compared to native reptiles and amphibians. Despite being a omnivorous species, they tend to be carnivorous. Therefore, they pose a threat to local species by predation and habitat competition.
A_Diet: Arthropods, annelids, fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and plants.
A_Crisis: An invasive species that threatens the survival of native animals.

A_Distribution: Central and South America. From Mexico in Central America through to Paraguay in South America and the West Indies.
A_Habitat: Living in tropical rainforests nearby rivers.
A_Feature: The Green Iguana has thick, strong body with a long, thin, and flattened tail. There is a large round scale on each side of the lower jaw. The ear openings are  distinct. The dewlap is retractable. A row of comb-like toothed scales extend from the back of the neck down to the tail. The limbs are strong and powerful. The whole body color is green, with several pale black horizontal stripes on the sides and the tail.
A_Behavior: Green Iguanas were originally found in Central and South America. These slender animals can move swiftly. Juveniles are omnivorous while adults are herbivorous. After captive-bred green iguanas were allowed to be imported into Taiwan in 2001, excessive import caused some individuals to be dumped in the wild where invasive populations were soon established. In 2014, this species was removed from the Wildlife Conservation Act. They have now been designated as a non-native terrestrial wild animal harmful to the ecology and environment.
A_Diet: Juveniles are omnivorous while adults are herbivorous
A_Crisis: An invasive species that threatens the survival of native animals.

A_Distribution: Emerald Green Tree Frog is endemic to Taiwan. Found in Taipei, Yilan, and Taoyuan.
A_Habitat: Living in broadleaf forests, orchards, tea plantations, bamboo groves, and other cultivated land in low-altitude mountains.
A_Feature: Emerald Green Tree Frog has slender body. It bear prominent supratympanic folds. The dorsum skin is covered with granules. The discs are well-developed on the finger and toe tips. The iris and  supratympanic folds are golden. The body is emerald-green or yellowish-green. A white stripe runs along each side of the body from the snout to the thigh. There are dark spots on each side of the body and on hindlimbs. The ventrum is white.
A_Behavior: Emerald Green Tree Frogs are nocturnal. It is shown that they are adapting to environments subject to human disturbance in recent years. During the breeding season, they can be found often in cultivated lands such as orchards and vegetable farms; they will also use the farmers’ water barrels to make foam nests.
A_Diet: Diet consists mainly of small arthropods.

A_Distribution: Endemic subspecies to Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Living in the forest floor, bush, grassland, and farmland of lowlands as well as low- and mid-altitude mountains.
A_Feature: Taiwan Beauty Snake has a thick, long and strong body and a slender tail. There is a black longitudinal stripe behind the eye. The body is a yellowish-brown or olive-brown colored. Four rows of black diamond markings run from the neck to the middle-section of  the back before converging into a dark-brown longitudinal stripe that continues to the tip of the tail. ; there are two yellow longitudinal stripes at the rear section. The ventrum is yellowish-white or grayish-white.
A_Behavior: Taiwan Beauty Snakes are diurnal and oviparous. They usually appear in forests, grassland, farmland, or near houses. This species is active during day and night. They have a tame and placid temperament.
A_Diet: Taiwan Beauty Snakes feed on a variety of foods including frogs, birds, small mammals, and bird eggs.

A_Distribution: Found in Kinmen islands, Southeast Asia and southern China. An invasive species in the southern US where it imposes great impact on the local ecology.
A_Habitat: The Burmese Python is mainly found in woodlands including mangroves and rainforests. It may also be found in grasslands, swamps, streams, and ponds.
A_Feature: The Burmese Python has a stout body, with a slender, triangular head. The entire body is covered with smooth, polished scales. The tail is short. There is an arrow-shaped dark brown pattern on the top of the head. The dorsum are yellowish-brown or grayish-brown and covered in large, irregular dark-brown saddle markings. There is a row of smaller dark-brown spots on each side of the body. The ventrum is white.
A_Behavior: Burmese Python is a nocturnal species. In Kinmen islands, they often inhabit areas free of human disturbance such as abandoned bunkers. Early in 1950, there has been a record of Burmese Python in Kinmen. Burmese Pythons are able swimmers so they can move and spread between neighboring islands.
A_Diet: Reptiles, birds, and mammals.
A_Crisis: Habitat loss and the pressure from the hunting for the leather trade.

A_Distribution: Only found in central Myanmar, South Asia.
A_Habitat: Arid grasslands, scrublands, and woodlands.
A_Feature: The carapace of the Burmese star tortoise is radiated- patterned in white color . The plastron of adults measures between 22 ~ 30 cm. Females are generally larger than males.
A_Behavior: Burmese star tortoises are most active at dawn and in the afternoon. The  monsoon comes to the arid regions of central Myanmar, the original habitat of burmese star tortoises, between June and September. The Burmese Star Tortoises become more active and start mating during this time. The females lay eggs between September and February during the cooler dry season. The hatchlings emerge when the monsoon return the following year. The herbaceous plants growing in profusion during the wet season provide plenty of foods for their development.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.
A_Crisis: Under the threat of being poached for the pet trade.

A_Distribution: Southern Papua New Guinea and northern Australia. Living in forest wetlands with sandy substratum,  such as swamps, rivers, streams, lakes, estuaries, and lagoons.
A_Habitat: Inhabiting the river basins near estuaries.
A_Feature: The Pig-nosed Turtle has a flattened body, short head, and large, bulging eyes. The snout is tubular like those of a pig. The carapace has no scutes and is covered with soft skin. The oar-shaped limbs have well-developed webs with claws.  The head and carapace are grayish-green or olive-green. The plastron is white or grayish-white.
A_Behavior: The Pig-nosed Turtle is a complete aquatic freshwater species that only comes onshore to lay eggs in the sand.
A_Diet: Plants, fish, mollusks and arthropods
A_Crisis: Wild populations are extensively hunted for the pet trade.

A_Distribution: Found in Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama in Central America.
A_Habitat: Living in the woods and scrubs near streams, rivers, and swamps in tropical rainforests.
A_Feature: Double-crested basilisk is slightly flattend-bodied. Males have three crests, respectively on the head,  the back, and the tail. Females do not have these crests. The iris color is orange-yellow, while the body is emerald-green or bluish-green, covered with numerous pale blue or yellow spots. The ventrum is yellowish-green. There are dark brown lateral bands on the tail.
A_Behavior: Double-crested basilisk can run at high speed on its hindlegs when there is danger. It can even run across water for a short period of time, so it has also been called the “Jesus Christ lizard.”
A_Diet: Arthropods, mollusks, fish, amphibians, reptiles, and plants

A_Distribution: North America.
A_Habitat: Living in larger rivers, lakes, and swamps.
A_Feature: The largest freshwater turtle in North America. The mouth is like an eagle’s beak. There are three rows of prominent dorsal ridges. The tail is quite long.
A_Behavior: Alligator Snapping Turtles adopt a sit-and-wait strategy for hunting. By using their pink tongues to mimic worms, fish is lured within the snapping range.
A_Diet: Fish, arthropods, frogs, and birds.
A_Crisis: Loss of habitat.

A_Distribution: Found in Southeast Asia from the Nicobar Islands in India, Myammar, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, through Indonesia and the Philippines.
A_Habitat: Living in tropical rainforests, grasslands, farmlands, wetlands, and nearby rivers
A_Feature: The reticulated python, with a slender body, is one of the largest snake species in the world. There are deep pits in the upper labiels. Three are three thin black stripes on the head, one in the middle of the head and the other two stretching from the eyes to the corner of the mouth. The back is grayish-brown or yellowish-brown and covered with a complex black, diamond-shaped net pattern.
A_Behavior: Adult Reticulated Pythons are usually found near waters and often lurk underneath the water to ambush the mammals that come to drink.
A_Diet: Birds and mammals

A_Distribution: The southern parts of the Sahara Desert in Africa, west from Senegal, east to Egypt.
A_Habitat: Living in arid grasslands, scrublands, and the borders of deserts.
A_Feature: As the third-largest tortoise in the world, African Spurred Tortoise is -bodied. The carapace is wide and tall, with the front and rear margins being saw-toothed. The scales on the forelimbs are large and overlapped with each other. The rear limbs have two or three distinct spiny protrusions.
A_Behavior: African Spurred Tortoises are good diggers and will dig dens to escape the daytime heat and freezing nights in deserts. They are generally active at dawn and dusk.
A_Diet: Herbivorous. Obtaining its water intake through food.

A_Distribution: Found throughout eastern China in Asia.
A_Habitat: Marshy wetlands, ponds, and irrigated farmlands in the lower reaches of the Yangtze River.
A_Feature: The Chinese Alligator is a relatively small alligator that grows to no more than 2 m. It is one of the few alligator species found in temperate regions.
A_Behavior: Chinese Alligators inhabit higher northern latitudes so they hibernate in underground dens in winter. They emerge from their dens in May when the weather warms up again. Breeding season usually runs from early July to late August. They build their nests from dead leaves and twigs, into which between 10 to 40 eggs are laid.
A_Diet: Carnivorous, feeding on fish, small mammals, birds, amphibians, and reptiles.
A_Crisis: Wild populations are threatened by poaching and pollution of their aquatic habitats.

A_Distribution: South Asia and Southeast Asia. From northeastern India and Nepal, through Indochina, to southern China, Found the southest in the Malay Peninsula.
A_Habitat: Living in the moist forest floor of tropical evergreen forests and deciduous forests in the mountains, hills, and plateaus.
A_Feature: The head is cream-yellow or yellowish-green. The carapace is yellowish-brown or olive-green with irregular black patches or spots. The carapace is highly-domed and oblong-shaped. There are large protruding scales on the forelimbs.
A_Behavior: Elongated Tortoises are opportunistic feeders in the forest floor. They eat not only plants and fungus but also snails and small invertebrates. They prefer inhabiting moist environments.
A_Diet: Omnivorous.

A_Habitat: Stationary bodies of water such as rice paddies, ponds or swamps at lower elevations.
A_Feature: The body of a water scorpion is dark brown and can reach up to 5 cm in length. Its flattened body resembles a dead leaf, and its forelegs look like two sickles. The water scorpion breaths through a long, thin tube at the end of its abdomen that can reach out of water for air.
A_Behavior:
1. It is a ferocious aquatic predator.
2. The adult attaches itself to aquatic plants and extends its breathing tube up against the surface. It lies in wait until preys come within range, then faces the target before attacking with its forelimbs.
A_Diet:
1. Carnivorous. Consumes bodily fluids of small aquatic animals.
2. Both the adults and juveniles will prey on aquatic insects, tadpoles, mosquito fish, and other small water animals.

A_Distribution: East Asia and Australia.
A_Habitat: Extensive distribution in the hills and grasslands of Taiwan. Most live in damp and shaded places such as rotten wood, rock crevices, and damp grass.
A_Feature: The Chinese red-headed centipede can grow up to 20 cm. Its head, thorax, first abdominal segment and legs are all red. Each of its body segment has one pair of legs. The pair of legs on the first body segment have evolved into large pincer-like "forcipules" with venom glands. It is a nocturnal carnivore.
A_Behavior: As a nocturnal carnivore, the centipede uses its forcipules to inject venom into the bodies of its prey to kill them. Centipede venom is similar to that of a bee's. Small centipedes only have a small amount of venom, so they are not threatening to humans.
A_Diet: Carnivorous.

A_Distribution: West Africa.
A_Habitat: A species of scorpions native to rainforests and lives in cold, damp caves, leaf litter, abandoned termite mounds, or under rocks. They only come out to feed.
A_Feature:
1. It is one of the largest scorpions in the world with a total body length of around 20 cm.
2. Its carapace is black and hard, and its pincers are hemispherical with a coarse surface. Its body is also covered with bumps.
3. The tip of the scorpion's tail is dark red.
4. The scorpion has four pairs of legs for walking, and the last segment of its abdomen has a venomous stinger. The scorpion's venom is produced in the last abdomenal segment and discharged with the stinger.
A_Behavior: It is a nocturnal carnivore that lives on the rainforest floor and the edges of the savannah in West Africa. It preys on other arthropods and small amphibians at night.
A_Diet: Carnivorous.

A_Distribution: The desert regions of Mexico on the Pacific coast.
A_Habitat: The drier plains of Mexico.
A_Feature:
1. The spider has four pairs of walking legs. One pair of its mouthparts have evolved into venomous fangs.
2. The spider's body is black-brown and can reach up to 16 cm in length. The fringes of its thorax are yellow. Each of its legs has three segments. The uppermost segment is reddish-orange.
A_Behavior:
1. It is a nocturnal ground-dwelling hairy spider. It usually digs its dens under a rock or a cactus. The spider does not spin silk to build its nest.
2. The spider feeds on insects, other spiders, lizards and birds.
A_Diet: Carnivorous.

A_Distribution: All over Taiwan.
A_Feature: The dragonfly's body is usually dark brown or dark green. Its legs and antennae are slightly longer than other dragonflies. Its eyes are small, and its head cannot rotate freely. The dragonfly has gills on its abdomen that can absorb oxygen directly from the water.
A_Behavior: The nymphs of bog-hawkers usually live in water grasses of slow-moving rivers and ponds or under dead trees or leaf litter.
A_Diet: Carnivorous and feeds on small aquatic insects and their larvae. Larger individuals may also prey on small fish and tadpoles.

A_Habitat: From the plains to low-elevation wetlands, rice paddies or ponds.
A_Feature: The body of this water bug is about 1.4 to 1.7 cm in length and is flat and round. Its forelegs are sickle-shaped predatory appendages, while their rear legs have fine hairs used for swimming.
A_Behavior:
1. It is an aquatic stink bug.
2. Females lay several dozen eggs on the back of males after mating. The eggshells only fall off once the larvae have hatched, so as to reduce their vulnerability to predators. They are therefore also known as "carrier bugs".
3. With eggs on their backs, males go in and out of water to allow exchange of oxygen for the eggs, as well as to help the eggs stay moisturized. The young hatch after 1 to 2 weeks and are immediately independent.
A_Diet: A carnivore that preys on small aquatic animals.

A_Distribution: Colombia, Panama, Costa Rica, Brazil, and Peru.
A_Habitat: On the forest floor, with a particular preference for crevices.
A_Feature:
1. Adults can grow up to 6 cm in length. Females are larger and their abdomens are thicker than the males.
2. Adults have a pair of gold-colored wings but they cannot fly. Males have wings that are longer than those of females.
3. Juveniles are dark brown, with four to six yellow spots on the sides of their body. They are therefore also known as the four or six-spotted gold-wing cockroach.
A_Behavior: It lives on the forest floor with a particular preference for caves. They feed on the feces of birds or bats. They behave completely different from the cockroaches you may come across at home and play an important role in the natural environment as cleaners.
A_Diet: Omnivorous

A_Distribution: Extensive distribution throughout Asia, Africa, Australia and Oceania.
A_Habitat: Stationary or slow-moving bodies of water, including ponds, rice paddies, and irrigation ditches with aquatic plants.
A_Feature: The diving beetle is a common aquatic beetle. Its wingcase is either smooth or have indistinct grooves. The sides of the beetle's wingcase have orange-yellow stripes. Its body measures less than 3 cm in length. Males can be distinguished from females by their forelegs, on which a joint has enlarged to form a sucker.
A_Behavior:
1. Adults spend most of their time in water but will leave in search of other habitats when living conditions deteriorate. They are often found in swamps and ponds.
2. Adults can be found all year in Taiwan. They can live for two years or more when kept indoors.
3. Once females have mated, they use their mouthpart to bite a hole in the stem of an aquatic plant, into which they then lay their eggs. The larvae go through three molts and form a pupa on land at around three months of age.
4. The young usually overwinter as a pupa. Once they emerge as adults, it takes about a week for them to become sexually mature and ready to mate.
5. Its lifespan is 2.5 to 3 months.
6. When threatened by predators, adults emit a foul, white liquid from the side of their dorsal exoskeleton to drive threats away.
A_Diet: Carnivorous and preys on small aquatic animals.

A_Distribution: In undisturbed mountain areas below mid elevation throughout Taiwan.
A_Habitat: During the day, they feed on the sap of large Japanese blue oaks and Chinese cork oaks and other trees from the Fagaceae family. They may even live permanently in the tree holes of these trees.
A_Feature:
1. A large stag beetle. The long-fanged stag beetle has the longest mandibles of all in the genus Dorcus.
2. Its body is black. Adult males measure between 29 to 90 mm, while females measure between 32 to 50 mm.
3. Males with long mandibles and a body larger than 45 mm in length, have a small but distinct bump in the middle of each of its mandible. Smaller individuals have no such bump on their mandibles.  
4. Females have less pronounced eye ridges. There are tiny bumps on the outside of their wing sheaths, arranged in shallow longitudinal grooves.
A_Behavior:
1. Adults usually appear between May and July, but their populations are relatively small.
 2. During the day, they like to feed on the sap of large Japanese blue oaks and Chinese cork oaks from the Fagaceae family. They may even live permanently in the tree holes of these trees.
 3. They are drawn to light, so females often rest on the poles of street lights or the ground nearby. Males are also attracted to light, but usually hide in dark corners further away from street lights.
 4. It plays dead when threatened.
A_Diet: The larvae feed on rotten wood while adults suck on tree sap and overripe fruits. Adults particularly like sucking on the sap of trees from the family Fagaceae.

A_Distribution: Only found on Ludao and Lanyu.
A_Habitat: Adults are usually active on the underside of the leaves of West Indian holly, while their larvae hide in the stem.
A_Feature:
1. The weevil's body has circular or oval aquamarine spots. Spots on the wing sheaths may span across the left and the right sheaths.
 2. A member of the weevil family that everyone is familiar with is the rice weevil we can find at home. Most think that all weevils have a long proboscis, but the Pachyrhynchus weevil actually has short mouthparts. It is black all over and covered with dreamy Tiffany blue spots.
A_Behavior:
1. The wing sheaths of the Easter egg beetle are fused, so it can not fly and can only crawl. It is therefore always found on or near the plants that it eats.
 2. It is an insect that undergoes complete metamorphosis. The larvae live in the stems of the West Indian holly, while adults spend their time in bushes or on trees.
A_Diet: Herbivorous and feeds mainly on West Indian holly.

A_Distribution: Taiwan, China, and Hong Kong.
A_Habitat: Stationary bodies of water such as rice paddies, irrigation ditches and ponds at lower elevations.
A_Feature:
1. Adults measure 7.6 to 8.8 mm in length. Its body is covered with fine hairs. Its head is black with black, thread-like antennae. Its first body segment is orange-yellow. Its black fore wings are covered with tiny round dimples and fine yellow hairs. There are thin yellow lines on the edges of its wings. Its leg is black but the joints are orange-yellow. Its abdomen is black with two milky-white, oval luminescent organs.
 2. Females are slightly larger than males. Females are similar in appearance to males but have only one luminescent organ.
A_Behavior:
1. It lives in areas of low elevation. The larvae are aquatic and breathe through tracheal gills.
2. Adults are only active for 30 to 40 minutes after nightfall and generally fly near bodies of water. They emit light at a low frequency, forming faint traces between sparks.
A_Diet: Carnivorous and feeds on aquatic snails.

A_Distribution: Malay Peninsula, Singapore, Thailand, and Sumatra.
A_Feature: The Malaysian stick insect is one of the larger stick insect species. Females have a bigger and a more flattened body than the males. The body of this species is covered with tiny spines, so the stick insect will raise its spiny hind legs while making warning sounds when threatened to fend off enemies. Raising its hind legs also reveals the warning color on its hind wings. Females lay large eggs in the soil.

A_Distribution: Only on the Henchun Peninsula and Ludao.
A_Habitat: Spends all of its life in screw pine bushes.
A_Feature: Females appear oily green and the nota has many small bumps. Its forewings are prominent and the hindwings extend to the 3rd or 4th segment of the abdomen. The opisthogonia is almost white with a slight pale green or pale rose tint. Its tail hairs are coarse and short.
A_Behavior:
1. It is endemic to Taiwan and has a very small distribution. It is threatened by habitat destruction and is being captured for trade.
2. It reproduces via parthenogenesis. A single female can lay between 50 to 70 eggs. The incubation period is between 90 to 150 days. Nymphs may emerge at any time of the year, but adults only come out between March and December. The peak is between May and October.
3. It is a species that undergoes incomplete metamorphosis. Nymphs usually need to molt six times to reach maturity. They have short wings but are flightless, so their population is geographically confined.
4. It is physically thicker and stronger than ordinary stick insects. Its body color is similar to that of screw pine leaves. During the daytime, it rests with its limbs folded flat against the leaf sheath, making it very hard to detect. It is mainly active at night and feeds on screw pine leaves.
5. It uses a very effective defensive mechanism to deter enemies; when threatened, it squirts a milky white liquid containing actinidine from the glands on either side of its pronotum. Some have described the smell of the liquid as "minty" or" resembling to that of rotten milk".
A_Diet: Herbivorous and feeds mainly on plants of the family Pandanaceae.

A_Distribution: Only on Lanyu.
A_Feature: The insect's body is green, its pronotum is covered with fine bumps, its back is well-developed and domed, and its body margin is diamond-shaped and has distinct knobs. Females have a ovipositor that resembles a long sword.
A_Behavior: Adults appear between spring and fall.
A_Diet: Feeds on the leaves of plants from the morning glory family Convolvulaceae.

A_Distribution: In Taiwan, on the plains and mountains at low and mid elevations. Extensive global distribution.
A_Habitat: Grasslands, farms, etc.  They can be seen around street lights at night. They are also found among tall grass, leaf litter, in crevices, or farming areas.
A_Feature: Adult field crickets can grow up to 3 cm in length. Its body is black, and its wings range from brown to black, with yellow spots at the root of its wings. Its head is short and rounded, and is slightly narrower or the same size as its pronotum.
A_Behavior:
1. Males rub their fore and hindwings together to make sounds. They stay quiet during the day and hide in the grass. At night, they chirp loudly for courtship, warning, and asserting territorial claims.
2. This species was used for cricket fighting.
A_Diet: Omnivorous.

A_Distribution: Bushes or tall grass near low-elevation forests.
A_Feature: The katydid's body is green or brown. Its most distinctive feature is the two large black spots behind the insect's head.
A_Behavior:
1. Adults can be found during summer and fall.
2. Males chirp very loudly at night. It is silent during the day and looks like a leaf, making it difficult to detect.
A_Diet: Feeds on plant leaves.

A_Habitat: Where citrus plants (Rutaceae) grow or are cultivated, including urban areas with high levels of pollution and disturbance.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized swallowtail butterfly.
 2. The butterfly's dorsal side of the body is black brown and covered with scales; the flanks and ventral side are creamy-yellow with four black-brown longitudinal lines.
 3. The outer margins of the hindwings are wavy without distinct protruding tails. The undersides of the wings are black-brown, and the surface has yellowish-white stripes and spots.
 4. The costal margin of the hindwings have a ring pattern in the Sc + R1 cell. The tornus has a red spot with a blue stripe at the front.
 5. The undersides of the wings have a blue-fringed orange pattern.
 6. The surface of the female butterfly's wings has yellowish-white stripes with an orange tint.
A_Behavior:
1. Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. Adults can fly very fast.
2. It overwinters as a chrysalis.
A_Diet:
Herbivorous.
1. Larvae feed on a variety of citrus plants.
2. Adult butterflies visit flowers for nectar.

A_Distribution: From plains up to mountains with an elevation of 2,000 m in Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Mainly in broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. The butterfly's eggs are glossy white and of a spherical shape with a flattened base.
 2. The butterfly's first instars are dark yellowish-brown, and have a black head and yellow osmeterium; second to fourth instars are greenish-brown, with a black head and a pair of yellow flesh protuberances on the thorax; the fifth instars have a green, radiating pattern, pale-green head, and two black eye-like marks on the sides of the metathorax.
 3. The butterfly's chrysalis is attached by a silk girdle. It is green with a yellow dorsal stripe.
 4. Adults have black fore- and hindwings covered with golden-green scales. The costal margin of the hindwings also has golden-blue scales, and there are blue lunules on the rear margin.
 5. Medium-sized swallowtail butterfly.
 6. Males can be identified with the patch of distinctive brownish down on the inner margin of their forewings.
A_Behavior:
1. The Papilio dialis is a popular swallowtail butterfly due to the bluish-green metallic sheen of its wings. 
 2. Larvae have camouflage coloration. Its osmeterium is extended when threatened or disturbed. Larval growth is strongly influenced by temperature.
 3. Adults visit flowers. Males like to drink from puddles next to rivers.
 4. Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. It usually overwinters as a chrysalis.
A_Diet:
Herbivorous.
1. Larvae feed on the leaves of citrus plants such as melia-leaved evodia,  alianthus prickly ash, and citrus trees.
2. Adults visit flowers for nectar.
3. Primary host plants include orange climber, alianthus prickly ash, melia-leaved evodia, and glittering prickly ash from the citrus family Rutacea, as well as wax tree from the cashews family Anacardiaceae.

A_Distribution: It is found in the low hills in northern Taiwan as well as the offshore island of Gueishan. In western Taiwan, it is only found as far south as Hsinchu, and in eastern Taiwan around Yilan. Some populations are suspected to have become established in Taichung around the Dakeng region recently due to human intervention. This species is found in Kinmen and Mazu as well, both of which are islands belonging to Taiwan. Outside of Taiwan, it is found in South Asia, Southeast Asia, western China, southern China and eastern China.
A_Habitat: Evergreen broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized swallowtail butterfly
 2. Its body is dark brown and covered with bright, green scales. Its forewings are nearly linear, and the outer margins of its hindwings have wave-like curves. The tip of its M3 vein culminates in a distinctive leaf-shaped tail. The upper surface of the wings is black-brown and covered with bright scales. The costal margin of the hindwings has a bright, blue-green patch that is connected to the shiny green line in the middle of the hindwings. The tornus of the hindwings features an azure ring pattern. The undersides of the wings are brown. The outer margins of the forewings have a grayish-white band, and the inner margin of the hindwings have a patch of yellowish-brown scales. There is a series of azure linnules along the outer margins.
 3. The male butterfly's gender identifier is a tuft of brown down on the dorsal surface of the forewings near the inner margin.
A_Behavior: Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. It overwinters as a chrysalis. Adults visit flower for nectar, and males drink from puddles on the ground.
A_Diet:
Herbivorous
Larvae feed on the leaves of citrus plants such as Taiwan Melicope,  Thin Evodia, and Citrus trees.

A_Distribution: Extensive distribution from plains to low-elevation mountains. In Taiwan, it can be found on plains up to mountains with an elevation of 1,000 m.
A_Habitat: Where citrus plants (Rutaceae) grow or are cultivated, such as orchards.
A_Feature:
1. The great mormon's eggs are pale-yellow and spherical.
 2. Larvae in first to fourth instar resemble dark brown bird feces. In the fifth instar, larvae are green with pseudo-eyes on the thorax. 
 3.  Chrysales are attached by a silk girdle. They can be black-brown or green, with the ventral side being green and the dorsal side yellowish-green.
 4. Males are always black with no wing tails The fore and hindwings are covered with bluish-gray scales, and there is a red spot near the base on the underside of the males. There is also an orange-red spot near the tornus on the underside of the hindwings.
 5. Females come in three forms: tailless with white spots, and tailed with orange spots. The tailed type can then be further divided into those with long markings or short markings, forming the third type. 
 6. It has a wingspan of 100 to 120 mm.
A_Behavior:
1. Larvae have camouflage coloration and discharge a pungent odor when threatened or disturbed.
2. Adults visit flowers for nectar. Males drink from pubbles near streams.
3. Adults fly slowly and like to stay out in the sun. They can often be found flying over parks, schools, man-made artificial gardens and red maple trees.
4. Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. It overwinters in as a chrysalis.
A_Diet:
Herbivorous
Larvae feed on all kinds of citrus plants including Trifoliate-orange, Chinese Box Orange, Alianthus Prickly Ash, Tetradium glabrifolium, Glittering Prickly-ash, and Citrus.

A_Distribution: It is found mainly in areas of lower elevations in Taiwan, along with Lanyu and Ludao. It is also found in most parts of southern China, Southeast Asia, and most of South Asia.
A_Habitat: Areas with a variety of birthwort species (Aristolochiaceae).
A_Feature:
1. The butterfly's eggs are orange-red colored.
 2. Larvae have a yellow head and dark red body with a conical protuberance in its first instar. From the second to the fifth instar, the larvae's head is black, its body purplish-back, 3rd abdominal segment blue, and its osmeterium orange.
 3. Chrysales are attached by a silk girdle and have an orange-brown color. The mesothorax and the 4th to 7th segments all have a pair of plate-like protrusions.
 4. Adults' forewings are black, while their hindwings have pale pink and white spots. They also have a pair of wing tails.
A_Behavior:
1. The common rose butterfly (Pachliopta aristolochiae) is very colorful and the primary species of swallowtail on display in the Insectarium during spring and summer. You can see signs of its larvae by looking for dents on the leaves of birthwort plants, which is the larvae's favourite food.
2. Larvae have warning colors and can extend their orange pillar-like osmeterium.
A_Diet: The primary host plants include Yellowmouth Duchmanspipe, Zollinger Dutchmanspipe, Aristolochia cucurbitifolia, Pipe Vine, and Aristolochia kaempfer from the family Aristolochiacea.

A_Distribution: It is found in places of lower elevations in southern and northeastern Taiwan, as well as offshore islands including Lanyu, Gueishan Island and Keelung Islet. It is also found in Southeast Asia, Indochina Peninsula, and the Marianas.
A_Habitat: Mainly in coastal forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a large milkweed butterfly.
 2. The butterfly's body is white with black spots and stripes.
 3. Its abdomen is white with a black-brown dorsal stripe.
 4. Its forewings are almost triangular with a curved costal margin and rounded apex. The hindwings are fan-shaped or ovoid with rounded outer margins. The upper surface of the wings is white with a yellow tint at the base. There is a black stripe along the outer margin of the wings, and each wing cell has a pair of hollow white rings; the center of the wings has black stripes, and there are black stripes at the tip and inside the forewing cell. The hindwing cell contains cross-shaped black stripes as well. The underside of the wings has similar markings to the upper surface. There are alternating black and white cilia on the margins.
A_Behavior: Polyvoltine butterfly, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. Adults live in forests and forest edges near the coast. They often fly slowly over tree canopies and visits flowers for nectar.
A_Diet: Adults visit flowers for nectar. Larvae feed on the leaves of climbing vines from the Dogbane family (Apocynaceae).

A_Distribution: It is found on the plains to mountains of low and mid elevations in Taiwan. It has also been recorded on offshore islands such as Gueishan, Lanyu, and Penghu. Outside of Taiwan, it is found in South Asia, Indochina Peninsula, Southeast Asia, southern Japan, southwestern China, southern China and eastern China.
A_Habitat: Mainly in evergreen broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a large butterfly from the family Pieridae.
 2. The dorsal side of the body is black brown and covered with white hairs and scales. The ventral side is white.
 3. Males have milky-white wings, and their forewings have a large orange-yellow mark at the apex and a dark brown pattern on the outer margin. The outer margin of the orange pattern in each cell has narrow, dark brown markings. The wing veins are covered with black-brown scales. The tips of the hindwing veins and the outer margins of each cell have black-brown markings. The undersides of the wings are white. The outer half of the forewings and the surface of the hindwings are covered with thin, dark brown stripes. A dark brown stripe runs from the base to the outer margin through the middle of the wings.
 4. Females have pale-yellow wings. The dark brown stripes are more pronounced than those of males.
 5. This is the largest butterfly of the family Pieridae found in Taiwan.
A_Behavior:
1. Adults are fast flyers, loves to stay under the sun, and visits flowers for nectar.
2. Males drink from puddles on the ground. 
3. Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year.
A_Diet: Larvae feed on plants from the caper family (Capparaceae) including narrow-leaved caper, smallspine caper, capparis floribunda, and spider tree.

A_Distribution: It is found in the mountains of Taiwan at low and mid elevations. They have also been recorded on Lanyu, Ludao, Keelung Islet, Gueishan Island, Xiaoliuqiu, Kinmen, and Mazu. It is also found outside of Taiwan in southern China, Indochina Peninsula, Sri Lanka, and Sumatra.
A_Habitat: Mainly in coastal forests and evergreen broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized milkweed butterfly.
 2. The body, thorax and legs are black-brown with white spots and stripes.
 3. The upper surface of the abdomen and its flanks are white but could be light brown on some individuals.
 4. The forewings have a protruding apex. The upper surfaces of the wings are dark brown and covered with a semi-transparent greenish-white pattern. These form lines at the base and become spots at the outer margins. The Sc cell of the forewings contains bluish-white stripes. The ventral wing surface is similar to the dorsal surface. The forewings have a dark brown inner margin, while the rest of the wing surface is a dark chestnut color.
 5. Males have a linear sex marker from the base to the outer margins of the wings along the 1A + 2A veins. Pale-grey specialized scales cover both sides. There are alternating black and white cilia on the margins.
A_Behavior:
1. Both the adult and the larvae of the blue glassy tiger butterfly will play dead when disturbed.
 2.There are many species of blue tiger butterflies. In addition to the blue glassy tiger, the Insectarium also hosts the blue tiger. Both the adults and larvae have warning colors derived from the poisonous host plants they feed on.
 3. Adults fly slowly in the wild. They prefer open areas and flowering bushes.
 4. Adults migrate south in large groups during the winter.
 5. Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year.
A_Diet: The larvae feed on plants in the milkweed family (Asclepiadaceae), including ovate tylophora, blackened swallowwort, and broad-leaved indigo.

A_Distribution: Mountains at low and mid elevations in Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Evergreen broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized brush-footed butterfly.
 2. The body of the male butterfly is a pale yellowish-brown on the dorsal surface, with the abdomen being yellowish-white. In females, the dorsal surface is dark brown, and the abdomen is white.
 3. The forewings are triangular with the center of the outer margins indented. The male butterfly has a protruding apex.
 4. The hindwings are triangular. The upper surface of the wings of the male butterfly is orange-yellow. There is a black-brown spot inside the CuA1 cells of the fore- and hindwings, and a dark brown pattern on the forewing apex, outer margin and center of the costal margin. The outer margins of the hindwings also have black-brown stripes.
 5. The undersides of the wings are light-colored and lack dark patterning. The CuA1 cells of the fore- and hindwings also contain a black-brown spot. The spots on the hindwings are surrounded by an eye-like pattern. The center of the hindwings has a brown stripe extending from the tornus to the center of the costal margin. The apex is arched outwards.
 6. The upper surfaces of the wings of the female butterfly are dark brown. The central spot may be white or yellow, with several white and yellow spots on the outer margins of the forewings. Cell CuA1 of the fore- and hind-wings each have a black-brown spot as well. The undersides of the wings are olive. The central mark contains a dark stripe. The cilia is brown.
A_Behavior:
1. Polyvoltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year.
 2. Adults are fast and lively flyers. Their preferred foods are tree sap and rotten fruit.
 3. Female butterfly lays egg masses on the underside of leaves. Larvae are gregarious and live on the underside of leaves.
 4. It overwinters as a non-hibernating larvae.
A_Diet:
Adults are fast and lively flyers. Their preferred foods are tree sap and rotten fruit.
Larvae feed on the leaves of trees from the family Celtis including Taiwan hackberry, Biond's hackberry, and Chinese hackberry.

A_Distribution: It is found in areas of low and mid elevations in Taiwan. It has also been recorded on offshore islands such as Lanyu, Penghu, Ludao, Gueishan Island, and Mazu. It has extensive distribution in the subtropical regions of Asia, the Indo-Malaya region, and Australia.
A_Habitat: Open grasslands, urban forests, wastelands, and parks.
A_Feature:
1. Males and females have similar patterning. The body, thorax and legs are black-brown with white spots and stripes. The dorsal surface of the abdomen is yellow, and the flanks are white. The male butterfly has hairy forelegs while the female butterfly does not.
 2. The forewings are almost triangular, with the costal margin curving outwards towards the apex. The hindwings are quite round. The undersides of the wings are orange, and the apical area of the forewings is black-brown. Inside are white spots that form a diagonal stripe. Behind the black-brown area is a dark brown region that extends into the cell or to the base. The hindwings have three small black-brown spots near the cell. The margins have a black-brown border and contain white spots. The hindwing surface occasionally has a white stripe.
 3. The male butterfly has a black pouch structure inside cell CuA2 on its hindwings. The opening runs along the CuA2 vein. The pouch contains black-brown specialized scales.
 4. The undersides of the wings have a similar pattern to that found on its dorsal surface, but the white pattern is more developed. The forewings also have an additional orange-yellow spot at the apex. There is a white pattern on the pouch structure of the male butterfly's hindwings. There are alternating black and white cilia on the margins.
A_Behavior: Larvae of the common tiger butterfly consume alkaloids to ward off predators. The butterfly usually flies slowly and close to the ground in a straight line. This method of flying gives predators plenty of time to recognize and avoid them. The bright coloration is meant to be a warning to predators. If attacked, they will play dead and secrete a foul-smelling liquid, forcing the predator to leave them alone.
A_Diet: The larva's host plants include sillow-leaved justicia, milk weed, giant carrionflower, cynanchum mooreanum, blackened wwallowwort and other members of the Dogbane family (Apocynacea). It feeds on new buds, young leaves, leaves and flowers.

A_Distribution: It is found in the mountains of low and mid elevations in Taiwan. Those found in Mazu belong to a different sub-species. Its distribution outside of Taiwan includes southern China, the Himalayas, Indochina Peninsula, Sumatra and Java.
A_Habitat: Mainly in evergreen broadleaf forest margins and humid grasslands.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized brush-footed butterfly.
2. The prothorax has an orange-yellow pattern. The dorsal surface of the body is black-brown and pairs of pale-yellow brown spots run along the abdomen. The flanks are yellow-white and a pair of black-brown stripes run lengthwise. The tip of the abdomen is orange-yellow or yellow-white.
3. The forewings are narrow with the outer margins protruding outwards to form an arc. The central section of the hindwing outer margins forms an angle. The upper surfaces of the wings are orange-yellow. The outer margin has a black border with a row of yellow spots inside. There are short, black patterns on the cell side of the forewings and its margins.
4. The undersides of the wings are orange-yellow with the hindwings being a of lighter color. A black-brown wavy stripe runs along the outer margins while the hindwings have an orange belt inside the wavy stripe. The cilia are black-brown.
A_Behavior: Polyvolltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. It is a slow flyer that visits flowers for nectar. The eggs are laid en masse on the underside of leaves. Larvae prefer to live in groups.
A_Diet:
1. Adults visit flowers.
2. The larvae feed on Ramie, dense-flowered false nettle, oysterleaf, hairy pouzolzia, Pouzolzia elegans and other members of the Nettle family (Urticaceae).

A_Distribution: It is found in areas of low and mid elevations in Taiwan. It has been recorded on offshore islands such as Gueishan Island and Penghu. Its distribution elsewhere includes all parts of the Indo-Malaya region except for the Philippines.
A_Habitat: Mainly in evergreen broadleaf forests and coastal forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized brush-footed butterfly.
2. The dorsal surface of the body is black-brown with white spots at the front of the thorax and a white band at the front of the abdomen. The abdomen is white on the sides. The antennae of the male butterfly are yellow-brown at the tip.
3. The compound eyes have sparse hairs. The forewings are an orthogonal triangle shape. The outer margins are indented at the center. This is particularly pronounced in the male.
4. The hindwings are fan-shaped. The base color of the undersides of the wings is black-brown and the surface is covered with white bands, stripes and spots.
5. The cells of the female butterfly's forewings contain white stripes split into several segments by thin, black-brown stripes. The white central spot is arranged in fold lines. The discal have short white stripes arranged in curved segments. The inner and outer margins of the hindwings each have a white stripe. The pattern on the inner margin is a band while the pattern of the outer margin is white spots arranged along an arc. The underside of the wings are dark brown and the white pattern is present on the dorsal surface as well. A white line runs along the outer margins of the wings. There is a dark colored belt between the inner margin and the outer margin of the hindwings. The base of the hindwings feature black-brown hollow pattern and white stripes. Black crescent markings are located forward to the white stripe.
6. The upper surface of the male butterfly's fore- and hindwings each have just a short white band running parallel to the outer margin. There are three small white stripes forward of the white band on the forewings. The underside of the wings feature in addition to the short white band two white lines along the outer margins. There are alternating black and white cilia on the margins.
A_Behavior:
Polyvolltine, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year.
Adult butterflies are often active along forest edge.
A_Diet: Adult butterflies are often active on the forest edge. They visit flowers for nectar but will also suck on rotten organic matter and water. Larvae feed on the leaves of Buddha's lamp, Formosan gambir, Formosan wenlandia, common wenlandia and other plants from the Madder family (Rubiacea).

A_Distribution: It is found at low and mid elevations in Taiwan. It is also recorded on offshore islands including Lanyu, Penghu, Ludao, Gueishan Island, Keelung Islet, Dongsha Island, Kinmen and Mazu. Its distribution elsewhere includes western China, southern China, eastern China, South Asia, the Himalayas, Indochina Peninsula, Southeast Asia, and Australia.
A_Habitat: Mainly in open areas such as the forest edge or grasslands.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized milkweed butterfly.
 2. The body and thorax are black-brown with white spots and stripes.
 3. The abdomen is orange with small white stripes and spots on the ventral surface and flanks.
 4. The upper surface of the wings are orange with a distinctive blackening of the wing veins and surrounding areas. The forewings are black-brown at the apex. Inside are white spots arranged in diagonal rows. The hindwing margin is black-brown and contains white spots. The male butterfly has a black pouch structure inside cell CuA2 on its hindwings. The opening runs along the CuA2 vein. The pouch contains black-brown specialized scales. The undersides of the wings have a similar pattern to the dorsal surface, but the white pattern is more developed. The forewings also have an additional light brown spot at the apex.
 5. The pouch-like structure on the hindwings of the male butterfly is raised. There are alternating black and white cilia on the margins.
A_Behavior: Polyvoltine species, which means it goes through multiple generations in a year. Adult butterflies prefer sunny, open areas. They fly slowly and visit flower for nectar.
A_Diet:
Adults visit flowers for nectar. 
Larvae feed on Formosan swallowwort and Lanyu swallowart and other members of the Dogbane family (Asclepiadaceae).

A_Distribution: It is found at low and mid elevations in Taiwan. It is also recorded on offshore islands including Lanyu, Penghu, Ludao, Gueishan Island, Keelung Islet, Dongsha Island Mazu. Its distribution elsewhere includes western China, southern China, eastern China, south Asia, and Southeast Asia.
A_Habitat: Mainly in costal forests and evergreen broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. It is a medium-sized milkweed butterfly.
 2. Its body, thorax and legs are black-brown with white spots and stripes.
 3. The upper surface of its abdomen is dark brown, the flanks are yellow with white stripes, and a row of white spots on either flank.
 4. The forewings have a protruding apex. The upper surfaces of the wings are dark brown and covered with a semi-transparent greenish-white pattern. These form lines at the base and become spots at the outer margins. The basic pattern of cell M3 in the forewings are separated into inner pattern and outer pattern. The male butterfly's pouch structure has an opening inside CuA1 so that the venation next to CuA1 can be curved. There are gray specialized scales inside the pouch structure and near the opening. The upper surface of the wings is similar to the dorsal surface. The forewings have a dark brown inner margin while the rest of the wing surface is a light yellowish-brown.
 5. The pouch structure on the hindwings of the male butterfly is semi-circular, pale yellow, with a  dark brown tip. There are alternating black and white cilia on the margins.
A_Behavior: Polyvolltine. It goes through multiple generations in a year. It is a slow flyer that visits flower for nectar. The larvae feed on green wax flower and cowslip creeper vine and other plants from the milkweed family (Asclepiadaceae).
A_Diet: Adults visit flowers for nectar. The larvae feed on green wax flower and cowslip creeper vine and other plants from the milkweed family (Asclepiadaceae).

A_Distribution: It is found at low and mid elevations in Taiwan and on offshore islands such as Gueishan Island and Lanyu. Its distribution outside of Taiwan includes southern China, the Himalayas, Indochina Peninsula, Southeast Asia and southern Japan.
A_Habitat: Evergreen broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. Its egg is shaped like a dark green ball. The first instar is black-brown while the other instars are black. Thin, long spines with red base grow along the flanks of the caterpillar's body.
 2. The pupa has cone-shaped protrusions, and is black-brown with white-brown spots.
 3. Adult wings are purple-black. Its forewings have a thick, orange stripe running from the frontal margin to the center of the outer margin. The underside of the wings resemble a dried leaf and has similar venation.
 4. It is a large brush-footed butterfly.
 5. The upper side of its body is dark brown, while the flanks are light brown.
 6. Its forewings are hemispherical with a curved frontal margin. The apex is pointed, and the rear part of the outer margin protrudes outwards. The hindwings are round with a finger-like protrusion at the tip of the 1A+2A vein. The underside of the wings is dark brown with black-brown wavy lines on the submargins. The wing surface is indigo with a metallic sheen. Cell CuA1 of the forewings has a small eye pattern. The center of the eye pattern has a small, white semi-transparent spot. The intersection of veins R5 and R6 in cell R4 of the forewings may sometimes have a small yellow-white pattern. A wide, orange-yellow diagonal stripe runs through the center of the wing. The underside of the wings shows a distinctive variation in patterning. The basic color is yellow-brown or brown, and it is covered with a mottled pattern that varies in hue and color. In the center of the wing is a dark line that runs from the forewing apex to the center of the inner margin, then from the center of the hindwings’ costal margin to the finger-like protrusion at the tip of veins 1A+2A. Dark brown cilia.
A_Behavior:
1. The dead leaf butterfly is named because of its appearance, which provides it with an effective protection against detection by enemies.
 2. Larvae have long, thin spines and spurt an irritating liquid when threatened or disturbed It feeds at dusk and dawn so is more difficult to observe in the wild.
 3. The dead leaf butterfly does not visit flowers for nectar. It prefers to stay on the ground to suck on fermented fruit, urine or bodily liquids of other animals. When disturbed, it will shoot into the air and fly rapidly into a nearby bush to hide.
A_Diet: Primary host plants include Lepidagathis formosensis, Strobilanthes formosanus, Strobilanthes glandulifera, and Strobilanthes rankanensis. Adult butterfly feeds on rotten fruit and tree sap.

A_Distribution: The Camponotus habereri has been found in China, Japan and Taiwan. They are widely distributed in low- and middle-elevation areas in Taiwan. It is mainly distributed in East Asia. However, in recent years, they have also been found in Australia and have become an invasive species.
A_Habitat: The Camponotus habereri is a tree-dwelling ant that lives in forests. It also builds nests on tree trunks in mixed forests on the city fringe, urban green belts and on street trees.
A_Feature: It is a large ant with polymorphic workers. Small workers measure between 7.0 to 7.6 mm in length while large workers measure 12.1 to 12.5 mm in length. The head is egg-shaped. Occiput is smooth and the cranium is covered with short, sparse seta. The frontal lobe has atrophied into a plate that covers the antenna socket. There is a distinct frontal triangle. There is no obvious antenna socket and the antenna scrobe is indistinct as well. The front margin of the clypeus is smooth, protruding or indented. The median clypeal seta and a pair of lateral clypeal seta are present. The mandibles are triangular or sub-triangular. There are more than seven denticles on the mandible apical margin. The antenna has 12 segments with no distinct club. The compound eyes are large and obvious. There is no obvious keel in the promesonotum. The promesonotum is smooth with no sculpting. A pair of long, needle-like seta grow from the pronotum and mesonotum. The promesonotum is completely fused and there is no metanotal groove. The metanotal suture is present and the metapleural gland has completely atrophied with no orifices. Mesothoracic spiracles are present. Propodeum is smooth, unsculpted and hairless. There is no propodeal spine or propodeal lobe. The propodeal spiracle is elongated. Petiole has no peduncle and the node is triangular. There is no petiole spine or subpetiolar process. Tergite is smooth and unsculpted with seta of uniform length. The stinger has devolved and the acidopore is present as a circular opening with no seta. The body has two colors, with the head, mesosoma and petiole being dark red, and the abdomen gaster being black with light brown patches.
A_Behavior: It feeds on plant nectar, nectary secretions, or small dead insects in the environment. Teams of workers set out to forage separately. They will also recruit workers. It forages at night.
A_Diet: Omnivorous ant that feeds on plant nectar, nectary secretions, or small dead insects in its environment. Teams of workers forage on their own. They will also recruit workers. It forages at night.

A_Distribution: In stationary bodies of water with abundant aquatic plants, such as ponds and swamps, below an elevation of 1,000 m.
A_Habitat: Stationary bodies of water such as lakes, swamps and ponds.
A_Feature:
1. Its abdomen is between 63 to 68 mm in length, and the hindwings measure 50 to 53 mm in length.
2. It has green compound eyes with an H-shaped black marking on the forehead.
3. The synthorax and the first segment of the abdomen are green, the second and third segments are blue, and the remainder are all black. There are yellow spots on the sides of the abdomen.
4. Females are similar in appearance to males.
A_Behavior:
1. The nymph lives in ponds or swamps overgrown with aquatic plants.
2. Adults emerge between April to November. Males patrol the air above their territory
3. Females are usually only active around water when they are ready to lay eggs. The eggs are laid inside the stems of aquatic plants, algae, and inside the leaves of large plants on the surface.
4. Sightings have been recorded all-year-round. They are usually circling over water bodies.
5. The nymphs will emerge during both day and night. This is the most widely distributed and most adaptable of all dragonfly species in Taiwan.
A_Diet: It can catch small flying insects in mid-air.

A_Distribution: In stationary bodies of water with abundant aquatic plants, such as ponds, rice paddies and swamp,s below an elevation of 1,300 m.
A_Habitat: Stationary bodies of water such as lakes, swamps and ponds.
A_Feature:
1. Its abdomen is between 27 to 33 mm in length, and the hindwings measure 32 to 37 mm in length.
2. Males have red composite eyes, synthorax and abdomen. A black stripe runs down the center of the abdomen's dorsal surface. The wings are transparent with red wing venation.
3. Females are completely yellow except for a black line on the abdomen, similar to that of the males.
Males are almost completely crimson in color. On the dorsal surface of the abdomen is a fine black line. The wings are transparent with a bit of orange at the roots and yellow wing venation. Females are either yellowish-brown or brown.
A_Behavior:
1. The nymphs inhabit rivers, ponds, swamps and river paddies.
2. Adults emerge between March and November. Adult males often land on twigs or grass near water bodies to claim their territory.
3. Females hover over water to lay their eggs.
4. It is one of the earliest dragonfly species to appear in any newly-excavated ponds on the plains. It, along with the slender skimmer, are very common dragonflies.
A_Diet: Insectivorous and can catch small flying insects in mid-air.

A_Distribution: In stationary bodies of water such as ponds, swamps and rice paddies on the plains and mountains of Taiwan. It is more common in the east and south.
A_Habitat: Preferred habitats include stationary or moving bodies of water, such as lakes, wild ponds, streams, rice paddies and swamps. It is a very common dragonfly. Adults will rest on branches overhanging the water.
A_Feature:
Adult fickle dragonflies grow to 3.4 to 4.2 cm in length.
Male:
1. Its composite eyes are dark reddish-brown.
2. The final segments of its abdomen have 3 longitudinal black lines running down the dorsal surface. Its abdomen is reddish-brown with a black tip.
3. The central dorsal ridge has a black stripe. It is flanked by fine, black markings.
4. Around three-quarters of its wings, starting from the roots, is reddish-brown. The wing tips have a small transparent patch and wing venation is red.
Female:
1. Its body shape and color are similar to that of a male. Black markings at the center and on the sides of its abdomen are thicker and more distinct. Longitudinal stripes along the margins are particularly well-developed.
2. Its body can be either red or yellowish-brown. Wing venation is either yellowish-white or red.
A_Behavior:
1. The nymphs inhabit rivers, ponds, swamps and river paddies.
2. Adults emerge between March and November. They are mostly active around rivers but will sometimes appear around stationary bodies of water.
3. Females hover over water to lay their eggs.
A_Diet: Insectivorous and can catch small flying insects in mid-air.

A_Distribution: Algeria; Chad; Egypt; Libya; Mali; Mauritania; Morocco; Niger; Sudan; Tunisia
A_Habitat: Arid mountainous area
A_Feature: The coat is sandy-brown with a tint of red. The inside of the ears, face, flanks, and inner side of the limbs are white. With Long tails and small ears. Rams have a long, soft mane that runs from the throat to the forelegs. Rams and ewes are both horned. Horns on rams grow outwards then curving inwards again.
A_Behavior:
1. Barbary Sheeps live in barren, rocky and desert regions. Due to the lack of large trees for hiding, they freeze when they sense danger.
2. They gain water from plants and dew in the arid habitat. 
3. They usually form small herds which are led by one ram and consist of several ewes and their lambs.
3. Since the Barbary Sheep were introduced to California, New Mexico, and Texas in the US, they competes with the native Bighorn Sheep (Ovis canadensis) for food and resources and leads to a serious impacts.
A_Diet: Herbivorous.

A_Distribution: South Africa; Botswana, Eswatini, Namibia, Uganda, Zimbabwe have reintroduced population; Kenya and the Republic of Zambia have assisted colonisation.
A_Habitat: The White Rhinoceros livs in flat terrain dense scrub with food, and water source.
A_Feature: The coat ranges from sandy-brown to gray in color. The ears and tail are fringed with stiff bristles while the other parts are hairless. The upper lip is square. The stout body has short legs and a thick, rough hide.
A_Behavior:
1. The name comes from the Dutch word wijd meaning “wide,” a reference to their wide, flat lips. This was later misinterpreted as “white” hence the name “White Rhinoceros.” It is also known as the “Square-lipped Rhinoceros.” Their wide, square lips eat grass like a lawn-mower.
2. White rhinoceros has poor eyesight. They depend mainly on their hearing and smelling. They can also run reach a speed of 40km/h. White rhinoceros usually are more placid and less aggressive than the Black rhinoceros.
3. Most white rhinoceroses live in herds that consist of female rhinos and their calf. Adult males are mostly solitary. They mark their territories by spraying urine and feces. Males fight each other with their horns for territory.
4. Mostly active at dawn, dusk and at night. During the day, they rest in the shade or soak in water.
A_Diet: Herbivorous. Mainly grass.

A_Distribution: Eastern Madagascar.
A_Habitat: Low-to-mid elevation primary forest with tall trees with broad crowns.
A_Feature: Black-and-white ruffed lemurs are the largest lemurs. Their ears and parts of neck are covered with long, dense, white fur giving rise to the "Black-and-white ruffed” part of their name. The main color of the fur on body face is black. The limbs, back, and the head are covered with white patches. There are four subspecies located in different area and different black and white colored patterns.
A_Behavior:
1. Black-and-white ruffed Llemurs are diurnal and are mainly active at dawn and dusk. They are most active between 5 to 7 pm in the evening.
2. Being arboreal primates, they move with ease through the branches and use a loud, distinctive call to announce their territory. Their larger size makes them must take extra care when moving in the trees.
3. They are social animals. Female lemurs build nests to raise their offspring. There are usually one to two per litter. Insted of huging mother all the time, newborn lemurs are placed in the nest and picked up by their mother’s mouth during movement.
A_Diet: Mainly eats fruit, seeds, leaves, and pollen.

A_Distribution: From Ethiopia and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo to South Africa
A_Habitat: Open terrain.
A_Feature:
Common elands are sexually dimorphic. Females are tan-brown with vertical white stripes and the dewlap is not pronounced. Males have a tuft of darker fur on their foreheads and have a bluish-gray color.  Their skin tend towards dark-gray as they grow older. The white stripes are less distinct and the dewlap is more pronounced than the females.
Their horns have a slight spiral shape. Male horns are thicker and shorter.
A_Behavior:
1. Social animals that mainly live on the savanna and open forests. They are non-territorial. Dawn and night-time are when they foraging and move around. If the weather is too hot then they hide in the shade.
2. There is a hierarchy among the males in the herd. Only high-ranking males have breeding rights.
A_Diet: Herbivorous. Likes to eat leaves and juicy fruit. Will also eat grass and tree roots.

A_Distribution: Olive Baboons are the most extensively distributed of the baboons. The range extends westwards to southern Mauritania and Mali, eastwards to Ethiopia and Somalia, southwards to Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania.
A_Habitat: Habitats include the savanna, grasslands, open forests, and gravel mountains.
A_Feature: The coat is olive in color while the face is black and naked. The coat is longer around the neck and shoulders of males, and they are also stronger. The muzzle is elongated like that of a dog and the tail is an upside-down U-shape.
A_Behavior:
1. They are diurnal animals mainly live on the savanna, grasslands, open forests, and gravel mountains. At night, it sleeps on trees or cliffsides. It is usually terrestrial but can climb trees.
2. Social animals that usually have 30 to 60 individuals per group. There are more female baboons in the group but the males have a higher status. Male baboons use fights and alliances to decide their respective places in the hierarchy. Only high-ranking male baboons can mate with female baboons in heat. The alfa (top-ranking) male is the group leader and decides the group’s movements. 
3. There are large numbers of baboons in Africa with a very wide distribution. Local farmers often have conflicts with baboons because baboons eat their crops.
A_Diet: Omnivorous. Eats various parts of different plants (the fruit, seed, rhizome, root, leaf, flower) as well as invertebrates, reptiles, birds, and small mammals. They are opportunist and eat whatever is convenient and in plentiful supply.

A_Distribution: Cameroon, Central African Republic (CAR),  Republic of Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Democratic Republic of Congo.
A_Habitat: Gorillas inhabit tropical rainforests. They can be found in mountain rainforests and bamboo groves from the lowlands up to an altitude of 3,000m. They prefer to live on the edge of forests near rivers in secondary forests. They are generally terrestrial but are good climbers. They are not swimmers however and even avoid forging in relatively shallow streams.
A_Feature: Gorila has no whiskers on their face. The fur ranges from gray to inky-black in color. Adult males having silver-white fur on the back are called "silverback"; short nose and muzzle, small eyes and ears, and large nostrils. The forearm is shorter than the upper arm and the palms are large. The body is strong and solidly built.
A_Behavior:
1. Gorilla collects and handles food with their dexterous hands.
2. They forage and move during the day. At night, female and young gorillas build a nest out of leaves and twigs in the tree to sleep in. The heavier males generally nest on the ground. A nest is usually used for one night then abandoned. 
3. They are social animals with 2 to 37 individuals per group. They are led by an adult silverback whose son usually inherits leadership of the group after several years. Gorillas form very stable groups. The members are also closer to each other than Chimpanzees. Young male gorillas usually leave the mother group when they become adult. They live by themselves until he can attract a female willing to form a family group with him. Female gorillas also leave the group they grew up in to join another group or start a few families with a solitary male.
4. When threatened, it will roar loudly, stand up and beat its chest, as well as rush around breaking branches to intimidate the enemy.
5. The longest period that a gorilla was kept in captivity was 60 years.
A_Diet: Omnivorous. Mainly eats plants with 85% of its diet made up of leaves, stems, and buds. Roots, flowers, fruits, and insects are also consumed.

A_Distribution: South of the Sahara Desert to Zimbabwe.
A_Habitat: African elephants can survive in the forest, grassland, tropical savanna with sparse trees, or even semi-desert regions.
A_Feature:
African elephants have a large head, short neck, with a massive body. Their limbs are long and cylindrical while the feet are short and flat. The soles are covered with elastic tissue to support the weight of the body. There is a tuft of loose fur on the end of the tail.
