A_Diet: Feeds mainly on small or mid-sized mammals such as wild hares. They will also catch pheasants, partridges, lizards, snakes, and even fish.

A_Distribution: Java in Indonesia and nearby islands.
A_Habitat: Forests or coastal plains.
A_Feature:
1. Males measure between 65 to 75 cm, and weighs between 672 and 1,450 g. Females measure anywhere from 40 to 46 cm in length, and weighs between 485 and 1,050 g.
2. Males have dark-green plumage that is covered with multi-colored scale patterns. The crest also has many colors and the throat patch is quite prominent.
A_Behavior:
1. There are a four species in the Phasianidae family, which belongs to the Galliformes order. A fleshy crest, or a comb, is a common feature they all share. The male green jungefowl has the most colorful comb and throat pouch, which are bluish-green and yellow.
2. There are more than a hundred species of pheasantsc but the green junglefowl is the only one that can fly over open water. It lives in the forest or on costal plains.
3. Its nest is a dent on the ground under dense foliage. The birds may also nest in fern trees.
A_Diet: Very little is known but are generally thought of as eating insects and grass seeds. Mainly eats seeds, berries, tree leaves, insects and meal worms in captivity.

A_Distribution: Africa
A_Habitat: Lowland and river valley forests, with a preference for mature secondary forests between the sea level and an elevation of 1,300m.
A_Feature:
1. The head, erect crest, neck, chest and nape of an adult bird are a grassy green color. The rump, flank, and tail are shades of black with a metallic purple-blue sheen. The belly and under-tail coverts are deep black. The area near the eyes are white and there is a thin black line under the eyes. The eyes are brown with red eyelids. Juveniles resemble adults but the black tips on their primary wing feathers are more prominent.
2. Subspecies can generally be distinguished by the differences between markings on their heads. The persa subspecies has the widest and longest white line under the eyes (extending to behind the eyes) and the tip of its crest has a pale red hue. The zenkeri subspecies has a narrow and short white line under the eyes while the tip of the crest has a pale purple hue. The buffoni subspecies has no white line under its eyes, or it is barely visible, and the tip of its crest has no pale pink or purple hue.
A_Behavior:
1. Active in the tree canopy and often slide along the tree trunk.
2. Female birds generally lay 2 eggs per clutch and may lay 5 clutches in a year.
A_Diet: All kinds of wild and cultivated fruit. They also eat flowers and shoots as well as snails and termites.
A_Crisis: The introduction of invasive species, resulting in hybrid offspring, has led to the gradual disappearance of endemic subspecies.

A_Distribution: The region between Indonesia and Australia including the Philippines, Nicobar, Papua New Guinea, and the Solomon Islands.
A_Habitat: Mangroves and lowland forests.
A_Feature:
1. Its body is plump and has a dark plumage. It has very unique draping feathers around the neck, similar to that of a chicken's. The upper half of its body has shiny dark green or copper-green feathers. Its undersides are dark green or dark blue.
2. Compared to a male, a female has a smaller the waxy structure on the base of its bill, shorter draping feathers, and a stronger brown color on its undersides. Juveniles lack the draping feathers around the neck and their plumage overall is a light, black-brown color.
A_Behavior:
1. More active at dawn and dusk.
2. Forages on the ground.
3. Their gullet is lined with chitinous plates that can grind up harder nuts.
A_Diet: Seeds, berries, and invertebrates.

A_Distribution: Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Australia
A_Habitat: Waterbodies of freshwater and saline water.
A_Feature:
1. Its body measures between 35 cm to 48 cm in length and weighs between 135 g and 250 g.
2. Its head is black with a relatively long crest. Its back is of a glossy dark-green, and its wings have fine, white margins.
A_Behavior:
1. Very territorial and solitary feeders that engage in “fishing” behavior.
2. Generally active at dawn and dusk.
A_Diet: Fish, amphibians, all types of insects, spiders, crabs, shrimp, mollusks, small reptiles, and small mice.

A_Distribution: Breeds in Eurasia and North America. Winters in northern Africa, India, and Myanmar. North American populations migrate south to winter in Mexico.
A_Habitat: All types of wetlands including freshwater, semi-saltwater and saltwater.
A_Feature:
1. Its body measures between 50 to 65 cm, and weighs between 750 and 1,575 g.
2. It has blue speculum feathers with a distinctive white border. Males are easy to identify by their bright green head and the white band around the neck. Females are brown with an orange-brown bill.
A_Behavior:
1. Very gregarious and will often mix with other ducks. There are very large populations in other regions and they can tolerate being in close proximity to humans. Their numbers in Taiwan are however limited.
2. Nests are built over grass on the ground then lined with feathers and down. Each clutch usually contain 9 to 13 eggs. Incubation period takes between 27 to 28 days. The chicks reach sexual maturity by the age of 1.
A_Diet: Omnivorous. They feed on all parts of aquatic plants and their seeds. In spring, they consume all kinds of terrestrial and aquatic invertebrates.

A_Distribution: Central and South America.
A_Habitat: Arid forests, open forests, and forests next to waterways in semi-arid regions.They do not appear in tropical rainforests.
A_Feature:
1. Its body is 70 cm long. Adults have green plumage with a hint of olive-green on their backs and wings. Its head is of a lighter shade of green than its body. The back of its neck has a slight pale blue hue. Its forehead and the exposed lore are red. The featherless part of its face is white and has a pink, fleshy look, with pale-green colored feathers forming criss-cross lines. Its throat is olive-green. Its lower black, rump and upper tail coverts are blue. Its underwing coverts are green.
2. The outer margins of its primary wing feathers are blue. Its upper tail is brownish-red with a blue band at the tip. The underside of its tail and flight feathers are olive-yellow. Its bill is grayish black. Its pupils are yellow. Its legs are dark gray. No information is available on juveniles but they may resemble adults.
3. The mexicana subspecies is similar to the type subspecies but is physically larger. The boliviana subspecies is similar to the type subspecieis, but its throat is pale reddish-brown, the base of its ear feathers are pale-red, while the outer surfaces of its primary wing feathers and the tip of its tail are of a darker blue.
A_Behavior:
1. These parrots fly from their roosting area to their feeding area in the morning. At night, they fly back to their roosting area.
2. Seasonal migrations are strongly influenced by food distribution. Paired birds usually stay together in a flock. The species will usually perch on top of prominent high tree (such as a dead pine on a canyon) when resting.
3. If approached, they will squawk loudly then fly into the air and show their yellow underwing flight feathers. They fly at a high speed with slow and shallow flaps of the wings.
A_Diet: Forages for seeds, nuts, berries, fruit and plant materialsproduced on tree branches.

A_Location: Bird World; Tropical Rainforest Area (Pangolin Dome)
A_Distribution: Parts of Papua New Guinea in Southeast Asia
A_Habitat: Lives in swamps, palm groves and more arid forests. Mainly found at lower elevations below 600m.
A_Feature:
1. Its body measures between 66 to 74 cm in length and weighs around 2,384 g. There are two subspecies.
2. The most distinctive feature of this species is the fancy fan-shaped crest. The crest is tipped with white spots. It is the largest member of the Columbiformes. Its plumage is pale, dark grayish-blue. Its chest is a dark azure color. Its speculum is light grayish-blue and dark purple at the tips.
A_Behavior: Generally forms flocks of 2 to 10. The male crowned pigeon frequently inflates its chest and flaps its wings in a display of aggression to establish its dominance. To court female crowned pigeons, however, the males nod frequently and wiggle its fan-shaped tail to try and win her favor.
A_Diet: Forages for fruit on ground, berries and seeds. They usually form small flocks of between 2 to 10 birds while foraging on the forest floor. They feed on fruit, plant seeds, mollusks, invertebrates, and crabs.

A_Distribution: Taiwan, southern China, the Indochina Peninsula, India, Papua New Guinea, and Australia.
A_Habitat: Mountain forests, orchards or farmlans of lower elevations.
A_Feature:
1. There are nine subspecies.
2. Its back is green and its neck and undersides are dark red. Its bill and feet are coral red.
3. Male birds have a silver-gray crown while their forehead and brow are white. Females have a brown crown and theie feather colors are less vivid.
A_Behavior:
1. They flap very quickly while flying and dash through woods close to the ground. They sometimes injure themselves through colliding with fencing wire.
2. Can breed all-year-round in many regions. The nest is usually a platform in the tree built from twigs. There are usually 2 eggs per clutch.
A_Diet: Feeds mainly on dropped fruit and seeds but will also eat insects, termites and snails. They usually forage on the ground alone or in pairs.

A_Distribution: Taiwan
A_Habitat: Flat lands to forests of low to middle elevation.
A_Behavior:
1. Constantly vocalizes while perched on trees making a sound like the wood tapping.
2. A hole is pecked in a tree about 2 to 10 meters off the ground to nest in. Chicks stay with the parents for some time to master survival skills before leaving the best.
A_Diet: Fruit and insects.

A_Distribution: Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Mountain forests of 200m to 1,200m above sea level.
A_Feature: It is a species endemic to Taiwan. Its body is covered with vivid, contrasting colors. Its plumage is generally a strong, deep blue color, with the area between its head and chest being ink-black. Its bill and feet are blood-red, and its tail feathers are blue. A_Feature:

A_Distribution: Grasslands, farmlands and urban areas in Australia
A_Habitat: Grasslands, farmlands and urban areas where there are some trees.

1. Its body measures between 31 to 36 cm, and weighs between 150 and 250 g.
2. Its head and neck are pale-grey, with a distinctive grayish-black crest on the head that can be erect or flattened.
3. Its wings have distinctive stripes and patterns. The genders are similar in appearance.

A_Distribution: Central Eurasia, stretching from the Black Sea eastward to Mongolia and northeastern China. They winter in India and the Sahara of Africa (from Chad to Ethiopia). There is a small breeding colony of the crane without continuous distribution in Turkey and northwestern Africa.
A_Habitat: Mainly found on savannahs, grasslands and other types of grasslands. They are mainly active around rivers, shallow lakes and wetlands. Some live in semi- or complete deserts with ready access to water. They can be found at elevations of up to 3,000m in central Asia. While wintering in India, they make use of farmlands there and nest in shallow water or wetlands. The crane prefers savannahs, grasslands and riverside wetlands where black locusts grow.
A_Feature:
1. Its body is 90 cm long, weighs between 2,000 to 3,000 g, and its wingspan is between 150 to 170 cm. It is the smallest member of the crane family.
2. Like the blue crane, which is another living crane species, the demoiselle crane's head is fully feathered with no exposed red skin. The nape and the tips of its primary wing feathers are black, and its white ear feathers extend from behind its eyes to its upper nape. The rest of its body is a uniform gray color. Black feathers on the front of its neck hang down past its chest. Its pupils range from pale red to wine-red. Demoiselle chicks are usually darker in color than adults, but is paler around the head and neck. Its ear feathers are not as pronounced.
3. Its call is low-pitched but sharp.
A_Behavior: Breeding takes place in spring around April and May. This can be as late as June in the north. Nests are very simple affairs built on open grassland, farmland or gravel. The nest is sometimes lined with pebbles or plant matter but eggs are often just laid on the ground. There are usually 2 eggs per clutch. Incubation takes between 27 to 29 days. Young cranes are light brown on the upper side while the underside is pale grayish-white.. The chicks become fully fledged after 55 yo 65 days, the shortest of all cranes. Sexual maturity is reached in second year.
A_Diet: Mainly eats grass seeds and other plant materials. They also eat insects. In summer, they eateetles, meal worms, lizards and other vertebrates. The crane walks very slowly while foraging. Large flocks form at stopover and wintering areas during the migratory period. They forage for food in farmlands, which is damaging to the grains and beans.

A_Distribution: Southeastern Russia, northeastern and southeastern China, Japan, and Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Lives in ponds, lakes, rivers and marshes surrounded by trees and forests.
A_Feature:
1. Compared to wood ducks, Mandarin ducks have greener plumage, less bluish sheen on their primaries, and smaller white markings around the eyes. Their bills are also shaped differently.
2. Chicks resemble females, although females have a pale pink bill.
A_Behavior:
1. The courtship display is very complex and refined. It consists of highly-ritualized waggling, drinking water, grooming and fanning behaviors directed towards a specific female.
2. Nests are built in tree holes and there are 9 to 12 eggs per clutch. The chicks reach sexual maturity by the age of 1.
3. Nests are built about 8 meters off the ground during the breeding season between March and June.
A_Diet: Diet varies according to season and where they live; in fall, its diet consists of acorns and cultivated grains. In spring, they feed on insects, snails, small fish and aquatic plants.

A_Distribution: From the Black Sea in the west, to Japan in the east, to the Caucasus Mountains in the north, and to South China and Taiwan in the south. In Taiwan, the pheasant is found in the western plains, the Lanyang Plain and the East Rift Valley.
A_Habitat: Its habitats vary significantly in natural environment. The pheasant is found mainly in dense foliage growing on river banks, mountains near farmlands, and flat farmlands.
A_Feature:
1. Males have a dark-green nape and a bluish-brown crown. A distinctive white band runs from the sides of the neck to the back. Males have back that is dark reddish-brown with black longitudinal stripes. The chest of males is reddish-brown with scaly markings. Their tail feathers are long, grayish brown and covered with dark brown horizontal stripes.
2. Females have light yellowish-brown plumage, with brown markings on the back. Their tail feathers are reddish-brown with dark brown horizontal stripes.
A_Behavior:
1. It is a subspecies endemic to Taiwan. It usually lives in grassy or farmed areas on the plains, hill, plateaus, or open river beds.
2. 8 to 14 eggs are laid per clutch with the female bird doing the brooding and nurturing.
A_Diet: Feeds mainly on plant shoots, berries, seeds and insects.
A_Crisis: Hybridized green junglefowls are considered auspiscious in eastern Javam which is why the bird is often captured and kept as pets. This poses a threat to their genetic diversity in the wild.

A_Distribution: Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka, and China.
A_Habitat: Open forests, bushes in the forest understory growing along rivers, or deciduous forests near rivers.
A_Feature:
1. A male measures around 200 cm in length and weighs around 5 kg. A female measures 100 cm in length and weighs around 3kg.
2. Males have a very distinctive crest while the females have a white belly.
3. Chicks are either dark brown or reddish brown, with light yellowish-brown undersides.
A_Behavior:
1. Breeding season varies depending on the geographical distribution but seems linked to the wet season.
2. In most parts of southern India and Sri Lanka, the peafowl's breeding season is from January to April; in the foothills of the Himalayas, their breeding season usually starts in June, but may ocassionally start in March and April.
3. Polygamous. Their nest is usually hidden inside bushes. In flood-prone regions, their nest may be built on high ground.
4. There are usually three to six eggs (and up to eight) per clutch. Incubation is about 28 to 30 days and brooding is done by the female.
A_Diet: Omnivorous.

A_Distribution: Western Papua New Guinea and nearby islands
A_Habitat: Lowland rainforests and mangroves.
A_Feature:
1. Its body measures between 66 to 75 cm long, and weighs between 1,800 and 2,400 g.
2. Its plumage is dark, pale grayish-blue overall. Its crest tends towards a light blue that is slightly more grayish than the body and has a silvery tone. Its wings and tail are a darker color. The back of its upper neck and its upper wing surfaces are a pale, dark azure color. The outermost greater coverts are white with purple tips and form a distinctive white patch when the wings are retracted. Its eyeline is black and quite wide. It has red pupils, a black bill, and dark red legs. The genders are similar in appearance. Chicks resemble adults but the wing markings are cream-colored.
A_Behavior: Tame by nature but will raise their wings to intimidate others of the same species.
A_Diet: Feeds on berries, berries on the ground, maggots and insects. They usually form small flocks of between 2 to 10 individuals while foraging on the ground.

A_Distribution: Taiwan
A_Habitat: Found in primary forests and mature secondary forests between elevations of 300m and 2,000m.
A_Feature: It is a bird species endemic to Taiwan. Its most distinctive feature is the bright white crest and back of a male bird. Males also have two beautiful long white tail feathers that are often worn on the head by the indigenous people of Taiwan.
A_Behavior: Polygamous. The male bird is very territorial so only one male bird can be kept per cage or they will fight to the death.
A_Diet: Berries, flower buds, tender leaves, insects (termites), and invertebrates (worms).

A_Distribution: Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Bolivia.
A_Habitat: Woods and forests.
A_Feature:
1. Its body measures between 38 to 42 cm in length.
2. Adults are almost entirely green, except their bill, which is gray, their forehead and lore, which are blue, and their pupils, which are orange-red. Their front crest is yellow with white tones. Their rear crest, eye ring, ear feathers, front cheeks, and throat are yellow.
3. The bend of their wings is red. The primary coverts are dark-green with purplish-blue tips. There is a dstinctive red patch that spans the five outer secondary wing feathers.
4. Their thigh feathers are green and legs are gray.
5. Its body has many different hues of yellow. Its upper tail and under tail coverts are pale yellowish-green. The base of its feathers on the sides of its tail has red blotches, while its outermost tail feathers have a blue margin.
A_Behavior:
1. They constantly shriek while flying, making it easy for people to notice their presence. They fly back and forth around their roosting area every day. They fly from the roosting area to the feeding area every morning then follow the same path home in the evening. They have two roosting areas in case predators discover one flight route.
2. Paired birds are easily identifiable when entire flocks fly overhead because they fly very close together. Sometimes, groups of 3 may fly past, but one is probably a juvenile.
3. Solitary birds or flocks of more than three are rarely sighted. Their body may appear red, yellow and green in the morning light but at noon, they become a dark silhouette.
A_Diet: Diet includes fruit, berries, seeds, nuts, flowers and leaf buds. Their foraging behavior may also cause significant damage on croplands. This species forms small flocks with the orange-winged Amazon parrot to forage in the treetops. They can often be seen foraging for seeds on palm trees.

A_Distribution: The distribution of the wild koala is from Atherton in the north to the coastal area in Victoria in the south; and from Adelaide in the west to the Eastern coast. This region includes Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia. Most of the habitat of this species was found to be fragmented and degraded, due to human activities and some natural disaster, such as bushfire, where the population has been split into small and separate colonies.
A_Habitat: Open eucalypt forest
A_Feature:
1. Weight: Weight gradually increases from north to south. Animals in the south are generally larger. In Queensland, average weight of male Koalas is 6.5 kg (6 ~ 8kg), while female Koalas weigh around 5.1 kg (4 ~ 6 kg).
In Victoria, average weight of male Koalas is 12 kg (9 ~ 15 kg), and female Koalas weigh around 8.5 kg (7 ~ 11  kg). 
2. Fur color: The fur darkens as you go further south. Koalas in Queensland have gray fur while those in Victoria range from reddish-brown to grayish-brown.
3. Paws: The first and second digits are opposite to the other three digits. The pincer-shaped front paws provide stronger grab. All the digits on the front paws are tipped with highly curved claws for climbing. The 2nd and 3rd digits on the rear paws are fused into one single digit (Syndactyly), which has a double claw on the top, and is used for grooming. Syndactyly is one of the keys used for identifying marsupials in the order Diprotodontia.
A_Behavior:
The English name “koala” comes from the Aboriginal language and means “no water.” Koalas get all the water they need from eucalyptus leaves.
They are arboreal animals and spend all of their time in the tree except for moving, breeding, or foraging.
They are nocturnal and spend most of the day time (between 18 and 20 hours) sleeping and resting.
Koalas are solitary. The breefding season is around spring and summer. Estrus cycle is about 35 days and ovulation  is induced by mating.  Gestation is between 34 and 36 days, with the newborn being just 1.9cm long and 0.5g in weight. The joey must climb from the its mother’s  cloaca and into the pouch where it latches firmly onto the nipple inside the pouch.
A_Diet:
Koalas eat mainly eucalyptus (gum tree) leaves. They tend to eat the tender leaves and stems. The eucalyptus is native to Australia and there are many species. Sometimes, they may also eat the tender leaves and flowers of other plants. Example: Paperbark tree (melaleuca spp.)

Examples include Lophostemon trees like the Boxwood and Bombax, well as the flowers of Stiff Bottlebrush.

A_Distribution: Red pands are found throughout Sichuan, Yunnan, and northern Nepal in forests over 2,000m above sea level.
A_Habitat:
1. Hu et al. (2020) separated the red panda based on genetic evidence into two phylogenetic species: the Chinese Red Panda (Ailurus styani) and the Himalayan Red Panda (Ailurus fulgens).
2. The Chinese red panda is mainly found in Sichuan and Yunnan in China.  The Himalayan red panda is found in Myanmar and Nepal, in mountain forests or bamboo groves between 1,800m and 4,000m above sea level.
A_Feature:
1. Red pands are 50 to 64cm long plus a tail 28 to 59cm in length, and weighs between 3.7 to 6.2kg. 
2. The fur is dark or reddish-brown. The color of its fur stands out in winter, making its coat look like a thick, red jacket. The short and stout limbs are black. The tails are marked with alternating brown (reddish-brown) rings.
A_Behavior:
1. The red panda likes to sleep curled up like a cat or dog with its tail wrapped around its head. It may also prop itself up with one limb and tuck its head between its legs while resting.
2. Solitary except during the breeding season. A female will continue roaming its territory with suckling young. It is most active at night or at dawn and dusk. It sleeps in a tree hole or on tree branches during the day. The red panda is an excellent climber but generally forages on the ground. It is quiet, placid, and curious by nature. When threatened, it will stand up on its hind legs while making a rumbling sound or snorting repeatedly.
3. A musky scent is released by the anal glands when a red panda becomes exicted.  It will also rub their anal glands against objects for marking territory.
A_Diet: Omnivorous. Diet includes bamboo leaves, bamboo sprouts, grass, roots, fruits, acorns, as well as insects, small birds, eggs, and small rodents.
A_Crisis:
1. The red panda is threatened by destruction of its forest habitat.
2. Traditional source of fur. 
3. Many red panda cubs die from Canine distemper and more than ten other parasitic diseases.

A_Distribution: From Argentina to British Columbia, Canada in North America.
A_Habitat: The Puma lives in a wide range of habitats, including high-elevation conifer forests, as well as low-elevation tropical forest, grasslands, and swamps. It is active from the sea level up to mountains with an elevation of 4,000m, as well as any region with suitable plant cover and prey.
A_Feature:
1. Male Pumas weigh between 53 to 100 kilograms, and females weigh between 29 to 64 kilograms.
2. The short, thick fur ranges from yellowish-brown to reddish-brown or bluish-gray. A white patch that runs from the throat to the chest and abdomen. The nose is pink with a black patch that extends to the lips. It has a slender trunk, small head, short face, long neck, long tail, and stout limbs. The rear paws are larger than the front. It also has small, short, and rounded ears.  The tail accounts for up to a third of a Puma's body length and is black-tipped. The broad paws have four toes on the front limbs and five on the rear limbs. The claws are sharp and curved.
A_Behavior:
1. The Puma isan excellent hunter with excellent night vision and a superb sense of smell for tracking prey in dense forests. It is also an excellent jumper, able to leap up to 6 or 7 meters from a standstill. The Puma can sprint very fast, but becomes tired after a few hundred meters. The long, sensitive whiskers are like human fingertips for sensing nearby objects. Hearing is very acute and the ears can rorate while hunting at night to locate sound sources.
2. Pumas are solitary animals. Males and females only stay together for a few days during the breeding season.
A_Diet:
1. A carnivore that mainly preys on moose, reindeer, and white-tailed deer, but will also eat rodents and fish. It also hunts smaller animals such as porcupines, sea otters, hares, snakes, and even slugs.
2. Leftover food are cached under rocks or piles of leaves.
A_Crisis: Threatened by land development for both residential and commercial use, as well as by the livestock industry, poaching, baiting, civil unrest, wildfire, and diseases.

A_Distribution: From Alaska, Canada, and the USA, to northern Mexico.
A_Habitat: It is semi-aquatic and can be found near rivers, lakes, and ponds.
A_Feature:
1.Beavers weigh between 13 to 32kg, grow to 74 to 90cm in length, and the tail is between 20 to 35cm long.
2. The beaver's rear feet are webbed.  The flat, broad tail is almost hairless and covered with scales. It has a pair of glands near its anus, which produces scented secretions that the beaver leaves on rocks or soil to identify one another.
A_Behavior:
1. Beavers use twigs and tree trunks to construct dams, dens, and canals.
2. Dams are built to create a pool of water in which the beavers can build their den, hide from predators, and store food. Beavers do not build dams in large, deep lakes or rivers where the water already flows at a slow rate.
A_Diet: Diet includes tree trunks, tree branches, roots of deciduous trees, and aquatic plants such as lotus buds. Tree branches are stored underwater as food for the winter.
A_Crisis: Humans hunted beavers extensively for their thick pelts and for the anal glands that were used as medicine or oil. Beavers were also killed for damming waterways use by humans. Populations are now in decline due to the destruction of wetlands, water pollution, and the construction of hydroelectric dams.

A_Distribution: Found in Asia, Europe, North America, and the Middle East. Mainly in the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
A_Habitat: Grasslands, and forests.
A_Feature: The gray wolf is a powerful animal with superb eyesight, sense of smell, and hearing. It is an excellent jumper and can reach up to 2.5m from a standing jump. It has a broad head, powerful limbs, big feet, and a deep and narrow chest. The heavily muscled shoulderws and powerful jaws allow it to rip and tear at the prey. Larger animals are brought down as a pack. Wolves can run as fast as 70km/hr to wear down the prey.
A_Behavior: Wolves are social animals that usually live in packs with 5 to 9 members. Each pack is made up of a mating couple, their offsprings, and their close relatives. There is a distinct hierarchy within the pack, and all members submit to the strongest among their number. Within a pack, only the alpha male and female are allowed to breed.
A_Diet: Carnivorous.
A_Crisis: Threatened by human activity and habitat fragmentation.

A_Distribution: Asia.
A_Habitat:
The seven Asiatic black bear sub-species are the Formosan Black Bear, Japanese Black Bear, Sichuan Black Bear, Ussuri Black Bear, Tibetan Black Bear, Balochistan Black Bear, and Kashmir Black Bear.
The Asiatic black bear has an extensive distribution that includes broadleaf and conifer forests, dry sub-tropical forests, and high mountain grasslands.
A_Feature:
1. Bears grow up 130 to 190cm tall and weigh between 65 to 150kg. Cubs weigh between 250 to 400g at birth.
2. The nickname "Moon Bear" came about due to white crescent shape on the chest.
A_Behavior: The bear stops feeding during hibernation, when all of its energy is supplied from stores of fat. Bears in some regions do not hibernate and survive the winter by migrating to lower elevations (e.g. Formosan black bear). Some scholars believe that bears don’t actually “hibernate” because their body temperature and metabolism remain the same. They wake easily and will move about if the weather warms. Bear hibernation should therefore be referred to as “dormancy.”
A_Diet: Diet includes fruits, leaves, flowers, honey, and insects. It is omnivorous but prefers plants.
A_Crisis: Threats include mass destruction of habitats as well as trapping and poaching. It is frequently exploited for medicinal uses in China, Japan, and South Korea.

A_Distribution: Native to North America.
A_Habitat: Ponds, streams, lakes, and slow-flowing rivers.
A_Feature:
1. The green skin is decorated with yellow stripes. The 16 sub-species  vary in their color pattern (For example, the Mississippi red-eared slider has yellow stripes on its costal plates, a distinctive yellow patch behind the eyes, while the plastrons are yellow with black spots.) Its head has a distinctive red stripe, while the oval-shaped carapace is usually green with pale stripes. Its rear limbs are webbed. 
2. Male turtles have a thick tail and particularly long front claws. Females are larger than males.
A_Behavior: Red-eared sliders are very adaptable and can survive in low-quality water. It prefers environments with silt and dense aquatic plant growth.
A_Diet: Juveniles are almost entirely carnivorous but become omnivorous as adults. Adults feed mainly on small fish, crustaceans, and mollusks such as crabs, shrimp, water snails, clams, frogs, tadpoles, and aquatic plants.
A_Crisis: The red-eared slider's popularity as a pet species led to its introduction to the rest of the world. It was introduced to Taiwan over 20 years ago, and breeding populations were established in the wild after illegal release or abandonment. As omnivores that can survive poor water quality, the red-eared slider poses a serious threat to native Taiwanese aquatic plants, invertebrates, freshwater fish, frogs, turtles, and terrapins in local ecosystems. The ecological impact is also amplified by its long lifespan.

A_Distribution: From northern Mexico and the continental USA all the way to western Canada.
A_Habitat: Grasslands.
A_Feature:
1. The American bison weighs between 450 to 1,350kg, and measures between 210 to 350cm from head to tail, with tail being 50 to 60cm long.  Adult bisons stand 260 to 280cm tall at the shoulders.
2. The head, shoulders, and forelegs are all covered in curly mane. The hips are relatively narrow. Males have fleshy shoulder humps that are less pronounced in females.
A_Behavior:
1. Bison live in large herds.
2. It has a good sense of smell and hearing. Herds are led by females. It can gallop at speeds of up to 40 to 50km/h. The migration follows a seasonal pattern, and herds may travel several hundred kilometers during the winter in search of better feeding grounds. It moves south in July in preparation for the winter, and head back north in the early spring of the following year. Bisons can charge at enemies with great force.
 3. Most active at dawn or dusk, the bison likes to roll in the mud or rub up against trees or boulders to remove parasites.
A_Diet: Herbivorous, the diet includes grass and tender stems. During the winter, bisons will root for mosss and dead grass.
A_Crisis: The American bison once roamed over a third of the North American continent but was almost wiped out by human settlement and mining in the Wild West. The U.S. government imposed an emergency ban on bison hunting in 1890. Reserves were alo established to protect the bison and Native American culture.

A_Distribution: The entire Northern Hemisphere, including forests, brushland, and rocky mountain slopes in Europe, Asia, and the northern parts of North Africa.
A_Habitat: The Lynx favors dense foliage in the forest understory, but can also be found in rocky areas or forests with sparse understory foliage.
A_Feature:
1. The Lynx usually measures between 85 and 105 cm in length with a tail 20 to 31cm long. It weighs between 20 to 30kg. Males are usually somewhat larger than females.
2. The Lynx has long, thick coat to withstand extreme cold. The fur is usually brown or gray, with some individuals having dark brown spots. The ears have white markings on the back and a tuft of black fur about 4cm long on the tips. The legs are long, and paws are covered with thick fur. Its tail is short. The legs have thick fur that allow the Lynx to move freely on the snow.
A_Behavior: Most active at night when the color of and the spots on its fur help the Lynx blend into its surrounding and sneak up on its prey undetected.
A_Diet: Carnivorous. In the wild, it hunts birds, hares, and rodents.
A_Crisis: Tthreatened by habitat destruction, poaching, and baiting.  The lynx is hunted in large numbers for their beautiful pelts but also killed for taking livestock. It is currently extinct in most parts of Europe. Fortunately, active rehabilitation efforts are underway in countries such as Germany, Austria, and Sweden.

A_Distribution: From southern China to South Asia, Southeast Asia, Taiwan, and Hainan Island.
A_Habitat: Low and mid-elevation forests.
A_Feature:
1. Same physical size as the domestic cat.
2. The body is grayish-brown in color and covered with dark, brown spots. There are two grayish-white bands with black borders on the forehead. The back of the ears are black with white spots.
A_Behavior: Leopard Cats are small, carnivorous felines that are generally solitary and nocturnal. Adept swimmers and climbers, they rest in tree holes or rock crevices during the day and only emerged in the evening to hunt.
A_Diet: Carnivorous. Feeds mostly on small animals.
A_Crisis: The primary habitat of the Leopard Cat are the foothill zone but these are threatened by human development. Partitioning by roads, vehicle traffic, hunting, competition and attack by feral dogs and cats, and disease all pose a serious threat to its survival.

A_Distribution: Southern and southeastern Asia.
A_Habitat: Extensive distribution in Taiwan. They have been sighted everywhere from broadleaf forests, coniferous forests, farmland, and hills at mid/low-elevations to mountain forests 2,000 meters above the sea level.  Frequently found in forests and irrigated farmland.
A_Feature:
1. The body is grayish-brown in color with a white stripe running from the top of the head to the nose, hence the name “White Nose.” A white patch runs from over and under the eyes to behind the ears. The conical muzzle has 40 teeth; both the nail and tail are quite long. The four limbs are short and thick, and there are 5 toes on each paw tipped with sharp claws. The unusual shape of the foot allows them to walk on branches or vines. They are the best tree and vine climbers out of all carnivores in Taiwan.
2. The anal glands produce very strong-smelling secretions that can drive away their enemies. They may sometimes emit a scent that smells like peanut oil when extremely tense, excited or angry. This led to the nickname “Black-footed Incense.” Scent is usually used for marking territory but whether it smells good or bad is highly subjective.
3. Though similar in appearance to the Formosan ferret-badger (Melogale moschata), the Gem-faced Civet is physically larger. The white markings on its forehead runs all the way down to the tip of the nose as well and is not interrupted like those on the head of the ferret-badger. 
4. The hooked claw on its digits are retracted when not in use and can be extended on demand. If the claw becomes blunt then it falls away under applied pressure. A new claw will then grow in its place.
A_Behavior:
1. Nocturnal and mostly active at night. Solitary by nature.
2. Arboreal and likes to eat juicy fruits, hence the common name “Fruit Civet.”
A_Diet: Omnivorous. Likes juicy fruits but also eats insects, snails and small vertebrates.
A_Crisis: The Gem-faced Civet features frequently on the menu of restaurants selling wild game. There’s a large captive population in the private sector and the pet market has many animals that were bred in captivity. Populations in the wild are under pressure from hunting. Escapees from breeding farms or individual animals improperly released in the wild impact on their gene pool as well, making the conservation of wild populations all the more difficult.

A_Distribution: Asia and Africa. Mainly in forests between 300 to 500 meters above the sea level.
A_Habitat: Low-elevation woodland.
A_Feature:
1. There are 8 species of pangolins in the world and the Formosan Pangolin is one of the 3 sub-species of Chinese Pangolins. It is the only member of the Pholidota in Taiwan and is classified as an endemic sub-species.
2. The body is conical in shape with a sharp muzzle, small eyes, and thick eyelids. The entire body is covered with grayish brown scales except for the muzzle, cheeks, lower jaw, throat, abdomen and inside of the limbs. Like other mammals the entire body is covered with hair. Even the parts covered with scales have 3 to 4 hairs growing underneath the scale. The four limbs are short and have 5 talons. The forelimbs are well-developed. The nostrils and ear holes can be shut. The mouth contains no teeth while the tongue is long and dexterous.
A_Behavior:
1. The word “Pangolin” comes from the Malay language and means “animal that curls up.” They instinctively roll up into a ball when threatened. The tail is used to protect the vulnerable neck and abdomen. 
2. Nocturnal cave-dwelling animal. It selects a slope with a gradient of around 30 degrees then digs a hole with its sharp front claws. Holes can be used for sleeping, foraging, and protection. The entrance is usually oriented in a southwest direction. Holes are dug by pangolins as a den or for food. Dens are usually deeper (3 ~ 5 meters) while those for foraging are usually shallower.
3. Pangolins prefer ants as well as termites living in dead or fallen trees. In addition to evolving features that protect them against ant attacks, they have a long, slender tongue about 15 to 25 cm in length covered in sticky saliva. The tongue can shoot out and retract around 80 times a minute to catch and eat ants. The Pangolin is toothless and food is swallowed whole directly into the stomach. The stomach walls are however strongly muscled and covered with a layer of cornified tissue. They also swallow sand granules that aid with the grinding of food. It takes between 3 to 7 days for food to be digested.
A_Diet: Feeds exclusively on ants and termites
A_Crisis: The scales are touted as precious herbal remedies in folk medicine so pangolins are relentlessly poached in large numbers. They live within 1000 meters of the foothills and this is where most of the over-development takes place. As a result, they’ve become very rare. The biggest threats they face in Taiwan today are feral dogs and animal traps.

A_Distribution: Found throughout East Asia including southern China, Taiwan, and southern Okinawa in Japan.
A_Habitat: Moist forest floor or around farmland on the forest edge of low-altitude mountains and hills.
A_Feature:
1. The body is rounded with the carapace forming a high dome. A distinctive keel runs along the center. The plastrons are not notched, with the pectoral and abdominal plastrons connected by tendons. Both the front and the rear plastron/carapace can move up and down. When faced with danger, the limbs, head and tail can be retracted into the shell. By contracting the tendons, the carapace and plastron can be closed off almost completely, hence its name “Box Turtle.” This is the only native box turtle species in Taiwan. Olive-colored head, yellow cheeks, with a yellow longitudinal stripe running from behind the eyes to the neck. The carapace is a dark brown color while the central keel and margins are yellow. The plastron is dark brown or black.
2. Tortoises are the only animals to have developed their spine into an armored exoskeleton. Most of their skeleton, organs and tissue are enclosed inside a thick, bony, shell.
A_Behavior: 1. Solitary and diurnal. Usual habitats are the margins of the forest floor or undergrowth, or near farmland where the ground is moist and near a source of water. They can swim but rarely spend time in the water. They will emerge after rain to hunt. At other times, they hide in the grass, leaves or crevices. The feet are column-shaped like those of tortoises due to the amount of time spent on land.
A_Diet: Opportunistic omnivorous that will eat arthropods, worms, annelids, dead or sick snakes. Diet consists mainly of plant roots, stems, leaves, fruits and buds.
A_Crisis: Due to the long time required for maturity, low frequency of egg-laying and small number of eggs, the number of breeding individuals have decreased in number; (more favorable conditions for raising young but also greater risk of extinction). When people started claiming that Yellow-margined Box Turtles have medicinal properties, or make desirable pets, poaching and smuggling (more than 6,000 animals a year at its peak) led to the rapid disappearance of entire populations.

A_Distribution: Southeastern Siberia, Korea, Japan, eastern and southern China, Ryuku islands, Taiwan, and Vietnam.
A_Habitat: Low elevations near water sources.
A_Feature:
1. The fur ranges from brown to reddish-brown in color. The back and the sides are covered with 7 to 8 rows of white spots. A black stripe runs down the middle of the back. The coat changes to adapt to the environment as well. In summer, it is made up of short hairs that are a bright, pale chestnut in color. In winter, it changes to long, tea-colored hairs with indistinct markings. The abdomen, inside of the legs and the area under the tail are all white in color. There is a large, distinctive white patch on its hindquarters.
2. The antlers of adult stags have 2 to 5 forks while does have no antlers.
3. Deer antlers are fully ossified and are shed painlessly in spring every year. The male Sika Deer does not grow antlers in its first year. In the second year, it grows simple horns. In the third year, it grows its first set of forked antlers, in the fourth year it grows antlers with two forks, and in the fifth year it grows antlers with three forks. No additional forks are added in later years (a few may grow antlers with four forks).
4. Antlers covered with a layer of highly vascular skin grow from the pedicle on the skull of the stags between May and June every year. This is known as “deer velvet.”  Once the velvet antler stops growing the blood supply to the pedicle is cut off. The velvet skin dries and falls off, and the velvet antler begins to ossify. The stag starts rubbing against tree to remove all the fine hairs. By the breeding season between August and October, the antlers have become fully ossified and are a grayish-white in color. Stags also developed long manes around the neck. Stags battle each other during this season for territory and mating rights. Individuals with more developed antlers have a better chance of asserting their dominance.
A_Behavior:
1. There are three species of deer in Taiwan and the Sika Deer is classified as medium-sized. 
2. They are quite tame though very sensitive and alert by nature.
3. Stags only start growing antlers in their second year. Their antlers gain one additional fork every year until they reach five years of age. The forks just diagonally outwards from the base where the antlers branch. Stags shed their antlers around May and June each year.
A_Diet: Herbivore that eats tree leaves, buds and grass.
A_Crisis: Sika Deer once roamed across the whole of Taiwan so it was once known as “Deer Island.” Dutch occupation of Taiwan proved catastrophic. They hired large numbers of workers and issued numerous permits for hunting Sika Deer. During Koxinga’s conquest of Taiwan and the Manchu Dynasty, deer skin was still one of Taiwan’s most important exports. Population growth and the conversion of habitats into towns and farms meant the last wild Sika Deer disappeared in 1969.

A_Distribution: Taiwan, from southern China to South Asia, Southeast Asia, and Hainan Island.
A_Habitat: Virgin forests more than 1,000 meters above the sea level. No sightings have been recorded since the 1970s.
A_Feature:
1. The upper jaw is quite sharp with well-developed canines.
2. The sides of the neck and body have large, cloud-shaped black spots. The abdomen and limbs are dotted with irregular brown patches. There are 11 to 14 black bands on the tail.
A_Behavior:
1. Nocturnal and solitary by nature. Adept climbers. Their short limbs and long tails are well-adapted to life in the trees.  
2. The Cloud Leopard was once found in all virgin forests above the elevation of 1,000 meters throughout Taiwan. This large, carnivorous feline is a sub-species endemic to Taiwan.
3. The animal in the Zoo’s exhibit is not a domestic Cloud Leopard. It is on loan from the European Endangered Species Programme (EEP).
A_Diet: Carnivore that feeds mainly on birds, primates and small mammals.
A_Crisis: Big trees are crucial to the survival of the Cloud Leopard. Taiwan used to have many broadleaf trees growing above 1,000 meters but indiscriminate logging of forests resulted in the loss of Cloud Leopard’s habitat and its extinction in the wild.

A_Distribution: Taiwan
A_Habitat: Can be found in mountain forests between 200 to 3,000 meters above the sea level and from the foot hills to 3,500 meters above the sea level. More common in mid- and high-elevation virgin coniferous forests. Often sighted near avalanche sites or steep hillsides.
A_Feature:
1. The body is dark brown in color with a black band on the back of the neck. The cheeks, throat and upper neck are a pale yellowish-brown. Tail is short.
2. Both males and females have boving horns. These are conical with sharp tips and are curved to the back slightly. The horns are not shed throughout their life.
A_Behavior:
1. The only wild bovine in Taiwan. It is endemic to Taiwan and was known as the Formosan Serow. 
2. It is a strong climber that prefers to live alone. It is most active at dawn and dusk. It is very territorial and marks its territory by rubbing secretions from the infraorbital gland in front of its eye all over tree branches or rocky outcrops. 
3. Can jump up to 2 meters high and run at a speed of 20 km per hour, making it the “most fleet-footed” of all mammals in Taiwan.
A_Diet: Herbivore that likes tender leaves and buds.

A_Distribution: Taiwan
A_Habitat: Found from the plains to 3,000 meters above the sea level.
A_Feature:
1. The body measures between 93 to 180 cm in length. Adults are dark gray in color and covered with thick bristles. The hairs on the back of the neck and the waist are slightly longer. The body is a round, barrel-shape.  
2. The neck is short with jutting snout. The front nasal bone supports a plate-shaped muzzle. The nose looks as if it was cut-off at the tip. 
4. The upper and lower jaws of boars both have a pair of well-developed canines, or tusks. Sows have shorter canines that are barely visible and three pairs of mammary glands. Juveniles are yellowish-brown in color with black stripes.
5. Wild pigs have an unusually shaped front nasal bone that form a plate-shaped muzzle. This can be pushed flat against the ground for sniffing. Pigs therefore have a well-developed sense of smell. Their long, jutting nose can be used like a bulldozer to turn over rocks in search of food.
A_Behavior:
1. Pigs will eat all the easily accessible food on the surface first. If there is not enough surface food, they start rooting around for food under the ground. 
2. Unlike other cloven-hoofed animals, wild boars are social animals. They form family clans led by at least one boar. 
3. Sows build a den before giving birth to protect the newborn piglets from the cold.
A_Diet: Omnivorous that feeds mainly on plants. Diet consists mainly of tender leaves, root tubers and insects.
A_Crisis: Wild pigs are now threatened by shrinking habitats and genetic contamination. Inter-breeding between wild pigs and domestic pigs meant the number of pure-bred wild pigs are on the decline. Taipei Zoo is working to preserve the pure-bred Wild Pig in captivity.

A_Distribution: Asiatic Black Bears used to be found all over Asia from Japan and China to Afghanistan and Pakistan.
A_Habitat: Forests between 1,000 to 3,000 meters above the sea level.
A_Feature:
1. The body measures 120 to 180cm in the length. The tail is 6 to 10 cm long. It stands about 60 to 70cm at the shoulders and can weigh up to 200 kg.
2. The entire body is covered with coarse, black fur. There is a tuft of short, white hair under the lower jaw.
3. There is a white V-shaped pattern on the chest.
A_Behavior:
1. The largest terrestrial mammal in Taiwan.
2. Very extensive range. They venture forth to forage for food in the evening or at dawn. They spend most of their remaining time resting in their den, in a tree hole or in a cave.
3. Walking with the foot flat against the ground is called “plantigrade.” Most other large animals such as dogs, horses and elephants walk on their toes, however, and this is referred to as “digitigrade.”
A_Diet: Omnivorous that feeds on fruit, roots, insects and small animals. Most of the diet is nevertheless plant-based.
A_Crisis: The main issues facing the Formosan Black Bear are habitat fragmentation (destruction of habitat), illegal poaching, and human interference. Black bears are highly dependent on the forest but roads often destroy the contiguity of their habitat. This not only reduces the number of animals that can be supported, but it also increases the risk of them entering fields or orchards on the forest edge where they may be hunted or trapped.  The “Leave no Trace” movement helps to reduce interference from human hikers.

A_Distribution: In parts of Taiwan with an elevation less than 3,000 meters.
A_Habitat: Found in broadleaf forests with a preference for dense natural woodland. Frequently found near bare rock or water sources.
A_Feature:
1. The head is rounded, the face is flattened, cheek pouches are present and the ears are small.
2. The back is grayish-brown in winter and turns olive-green in summer; the limbs and tail have a slightly darker color.
3. The abdomen is grayish white; there are red flesh pads at the buttocks; the tail is thick and long.
A_Behavior:
1. Diurnal animal that is mostly active at dawn and dusk. Lives mostly in the trees but will forage for food on the ground. Preferred habitat is dense natural forests and exposed rock with nearby water sources.
2. Social animals that form clans led by a male monkey. Clans have no fixed size but generally range between 10 to 50 members. A clan consists of one of adult male along with several adult females, sub-adult males and juveniles. Males living by themselves or in bachelor groups can be observed in the wild.
A_Diet: Feeds mainly on fruits and buds. Will sometimes eat insects and small mammals. The diet changes depending on the season.
A_Crisis: Human development and the continued expansion of recreational areas meant that traditional habitats and territories of the Macaque are increasingly overlapping with those of mankind. Humans muscling into macaque territory has resulted in a great deal of friction. The main issues facing the Formosan Macaque today are friction due to human occupation of their habitats and improper interactions with humans (feeding). The use of snap traps and other illegal traps represents a serious threat to wild Formosan Macaques.

A_Distribution: Forests of Taiwan with an elevation less than 1,200 meters.
A_Habitat: Broadleaf forests, hillsides, or parts of the countryside with dense foliage.
A_Feature: The eyes are orange-red in color and the tufts on the head are erect like ears. The body is grayish-brown in color with irregular black bands. The face is grey with dark-brown margins.
A_Behavior:
1. Lives in broadleaf forests at lower elevations. It lives at the lowest elevations and closest to human beings of all owls in Taiwan. Sometimes, they nest in parks or houses.
2. Nocturnal animal that spends most of the day sleeping on a tree.
3. Acute eyesight and the ability of the head to rotate through 270 degrees allows it to locate the prey with great precision.
A_Diet: Hunts insects, birds and small mammals.

A_Distribution: Western and northwestern Europe, and Asia; in Taiwan, they were originally found in or near rivers throughout the island with an elevation below 1,500 meters. There have been no sightings on Taiwan proper for many years. Small colonies were recorded in Kinmen.
A_Habitat: Otters live in freshwater bodies inland but can adapt to river deltas or seawater.
A_Feature:
1. The back is chestnut brown and the body is streamlined. The head and trunk are elongated while the limbs are short with webbing between the toes. The fur is short and dense. 
2. The whiskers around the mouth are tactile and can detect nearby disturbances.
A_Behavior:
1. Solitary and semi-aquatic animal that lives in inland freshwater bodies. They are very agile on land and in water, and are active during the day and at night. They are however most active at night and can range over great distances.
2. Otters build dens in embankments or grass near the water. They have a scent gland that releases a foul smell to deter frightening or threatening enemies.
A_Diet: Carnivore that feeds on invertebrates, crustaceans and amphibians in the water, as well as aquatic fowls and rodents near the water.
A_Crisis: Accelerated development, destruction and pollution of wetlands, blocking of water routes, feral dog attacks and road kills are all threatening the survival of the otters. There are now estimated to be less than 200 animals left in Kinmen. All of the above issues are human-related.

A_Distribution: Found on low and mid-elevation mountains of Taiwan.
A_Habitat: Can be found in forests and grassland.
A_Feature:
1. The four limbs are short with large, broad feet. The long, powerful talons can be used for digging.
2. The tail is bushy with long, white hair. The face is narrow and rodent-like with a pink nose. Rounded ears, short limbs, and long, thin sharp claws. 
3. The back is generally grayish-brown to brownish-black in color, with the abdomen being a slightly paler shade.
4. A white longitudinal band run from the head down past the neck and to the middle of the back. There is a yellowish-white patch on the top of the head. The area between the cheeks and the front of the neck as well as the middle of the abdomen are all yellowish-white too.
A_Behavior:
1. Social, solitary and nocturnal.
2. They sleep in a cave during the day. When threatened or stressed, a foul smell can be released by the anal glands to deter the enemy.
A_Diet: Omnivorous. Diet consists of small vertebrates, insects, worms and fruits.
A_Crisis: Feral dogs and cats spread rabies in the wild. Formosan Ferret-Badgers are easily infected by the virus.

A_Name: Small Chinese Civet, Lesser Oriental Civet
A_Distribution: Low and middle elevations in Taiwan
A_Habitat: Lives mainly in dense, virgin broadleaf forests.
A_Feature:
1. The fur is yellowish-brown with dark, brown longitudinal bands on the back. The tail has distinctive dark-brown bands.
2. Similar in appearance to a cat though the muzzle is more conical and the neck is elongated.
3. Both males and females have a musk gland that produces a very foul-smelling secretion. The secretions are applied to rocks or tree trunks as territorial markings.
A_Behavior: Nocturnal and secretive by nature. Generally leads a solitary existence on the ground.
A_Diet: Omnivorous that feeds mainly on small mammals, reptiles and insects. Can also eat fruits and young grass.

A_Distribution: Found in southeastern China, and throughout Taiwan from the lowlands to 3,000 meters above the sea level. Frequently sighted in broadleaf forests and water sources as well as Green Island.
A_Habitat: Found everywhere below an elevation of 3,000 meters.
A_Feature:
1. Small member of the deer family. Entire body is yellowish-brown in color with scattered black hairs.
2. Most males of the deer family grow forked antlers on their heads that are shed and regrown every year. Females have only bony bumps on their head and no antlers. Males have a pair of simply crossed horns. There is a small bump in front of the pedicle. Newborn Reeves Muntjac is covered with spots for protective coloration. These fade away after about 45 days.
A_Behavior:
1. Crepuscular so it can be active throughout the day, though mostly at dawn and dusk.
2. Very shy by nature. If there is danger, the first reaction is to freeze or hide. If a predator is approaching then it raises its short tail to reveal the white fur underneath before fleeing at high speed. It also issues a series of short, high-pitched, monotone calls that sound like a dog bark.
3. Male and females exhibit distinct behavioral differences. Male Reeves Muntjacs are quite territorial while female Reeves Muntjacs get on reasonably well. Between three to four female Reeves Muntjacs with overlapping territories often live within the territory of one male Reeves Muntjac.
A_Diet: Herbivore that likes to feed on the leaves of bushes and ferns, with a particular preference for young leaves and buds.

A_Conservation: (Taiwan Endemic Sub-species) Other wild life to conserve
A_Distribution: Taiwan
A_Habitat: Found in river valleys near virgin forests and high-mountain grasslands 1,500 meters above the sea level. More numerous in the Central Mountain Range and the mountains of Hualien and Taitung.
A_Feature:
1. The largest herbivorous wild animal in Taiwan.
2. The coat tends towards brown in summer and changes to dark brown in winter.
3. The tarsal glands are well-developed and there appears to be four eyes from a distance. It is therefore also referred to as “Four-eyed Deer.”
A_Behavior:
1. Social animal though the stags are usually solitary.
2. Most active at dawn and dusk. Prefers to eat and live near water sources on high mountains or grassland near rivers.
A_Diet: Herbivore that feeds mainly on arrow bamboo, grass, young grass and leaves.
A_Crisis: The Sambar has been domesticated in Taiwan for more than a century. There are quite a large number of animals in captivity kept for their deer velvet, a very precious traditional Chinese medicine.

A_Distribution: Eastern mainland Australia and the island of Tasmania.
A_Habitat: Sclerophyll forest, woodlands (including mallee scrub), shrubland and heathland.
A_Feature:
1. The Eastern Gray Kangaroo is the tallest of the kangaroos and the best jumper as well.
2. The body is gray in color and the muzzle is richly whiskered. Their hind-legs are well-developed and there is a long tail. Mature females have a well-developed pouch and four nipples.
A_Behavior:
1. Usually stands on its hind-legs and moves forward in leaps and bounds. They also move on all four.
2.Gray kangaroo has tight-knit social structure. The group is mainly made up of females and their offsprings each with their rank. Males only join the group when females are in heat.
3. They can breed all year-round and give birth to only one joey each time. A newborn will climb by itself into the mother’s pouch and spend over 9 months inside before leaving.
A_Diet: Herbivorous. Mainly eats grass and does not need a lot of water.

A_Distribution: Northern Australia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.
A_Habitat: Inhabitat in rainforest and occasionally using adjacent savanna forests, mangroves and fruit plantations.
A_Feature: A large flightless bird. The head and neck are hairless, the skin is a purplish-blue color, and there is a horny crest on the head; there are 2 brightly colored folds of skin on the neck. The legs are long and thick with 3 toes tipped with sharp claws. Adult birds have brownish-black colors. Male and females are almost the same size though females are slightly larger and have brighter colors. Fledglings are covered with dark brown and yellowish-brown stripes. The eggs are grassy green in color and slightly wrinkled on the surface.
A_Behavior:
1. Cassowary is usually solitary and lives in virgin forests. They are active at dawn, dusk, and moonlit lights. Territorial. The nest is a shallow pit lined with leaves and grass. It is usually built in dense bushland.
2. Unlike ordinary bird feathers, the feathers of the Cassowary are fluffy and fan-shaped. They are also stiffer than ordinary feathers to protect the bird from branches and thorns while moving through the dense undergrowth. 
3. The crest on the head of the Cassowary, called "casque", can be used to nudge branches aside in the dense forest, or help their very low frequency sounds penetrading through the dense forest.
A_Diet: Mainly eats fruits that fall to the ground but will eat seeds, insects, small animals, or carrion.

A_Distribution: Australia.
A_Habitat: Savanna, shrubland, and grassland.
A_Feature: The head and upper part of the neck have black feathers. Naked skin has a blue tint and adult emus are covered with a mix of grayish-brown feathers. Unlike ordinary birds, the feathers are loose to fan-shaped. The wings have degenerated to a small size and cannot be used for fly.
A_Behavior: A diurnal bird that can continue to forage even when it's over 40 degrees Celsius. Both hatching and raising young chicks are done by male. The male does not eat or drink while hatching eggs. It only stands up when the eggs need to be turned
A_Diet: Herbivorous. Eats fruits, seeds, flowers, buds, insects, or even bark.
